tvreleases.name: Project Full
tvreleases.body:
======================================================================
 RETRO VOLT SUITE PARA PLAYSTATION 2 - GUIA COMPLETO (LEIA-ME)
 FastLoader V2.1.1 - Retro Arcade V1.1.0 - Retro Volt - Suite (Windows)
 CRIADO POR RETROVOLT - LEONARDO TORRES - 21/10/2026
======================================================================

Este guia explica, passo a passo, como montar e usar a suite. Leia na
ordem na primeira vez. Depois use como consulta.

Manual completo com imagens (PT, EN, ES):
https://claude.ai/artifact/TbHwMBFJQS6zcHkxzZPuug


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 1. O QUE E A SUITE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  FASTLOADER       O menu principal do PS2. Lista e inicia:
                   - jogos de PS2 (ISO) do HD, pendrive, MX4SIO, MMCE e
                     do PC pela rede (pelo Neutrino);
                   - jogos de PS1 (pelo Ember);
                   - o disco que estiver no leitor (aba CDVD);
                   - programas .elf (pelo FILES).
                   Tem gerenciador de arquivos (FILES), favoritos, capas,
                   memory card virtual e idioma PT-BR / ENG.

  RETRO ARCADE     Menu de arcade e consoles, aberto pelo FastLoader
                   (START > Extras > Retro Arcade):
                   CPS1, CPS2, Neo-Geo (MVS), PC Engine e Neo Geo CD.

  NUCLEOS          Os emuladores de cada sistema. Ficam protegidos
                   (cifrados) junto com o Retro Arcade, como arquivos .SYS.

  RETRO VOLT -     Programa de Windows (RetroVoltSuite.exe): cria as
  SUITE            pastas, baixa capas, cria memory cards virtuais,
                   protege os nucleos e serve jogos pela rede.

  O UNICO programa visivel no aparelho e o FASTLOADER.ELF. Todo o resto
  e aberto por ele.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 2. O QUE VOCE PRECISA
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  [ ] Um PS2 que abre programas caseiros (.elf): FreeMcBoot (FMCB),
      PS2BBL ou outro launcher no memory card.
  [ ] Um memory card no slot 1 (guarda idioma, favoritos e ajustes).
  [ ] Onde guardar os jogos (um ou mais):
        - HD interno formatado em exFAT (o melhor);
        - pendrive em exFAT ou FAT32 (FAT32 nao aceita arquivo de 4 GB
          ou mais: DVD grande precisa de exFAT);
        - cartao SD no adaptador MX4SIO;
        - MMCE (MemCard PRO 2 / SD2PSX).
  [ ] O pacote da suite: Vxx_retrovolt_full.zip (o numero maior e o mais
      novo).
  [ ] NEUTRINO (obrigatorio para PS2): o pacote completo, versao mais
      nova (v1.8.0 ou mais nova se for usar a rede).
  [ ] EMBER (obrigatorio para PS1): Beta 2 ou mais novo, e a BIOS do seu
      proprio console (bios.bin).
  [ ] Windows, para o Retro Volt - Suite (opcional, mas recomendado).


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 3. COMO FICA A RAIZ DO HD OU PENDRIVE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  Copie exatamente assim. Maiusculas e minusculas nao importam no HD e
  no pendrive.

  HD ou PENDRIVE:\
  |
  +-- RETROVOLT\                         <- TUDO da suite fica aqui
  |   |
  |   +-- FASTLOADER\
  |   |   +-- FASTLOADER.ELF             <- o programa que voce abre
  |   |   +-- neutrino.elf               <- do pacote do Neutrino
  |   |   +-- config\                    <- do pacote do Neutrino
  |   |   +-- modules\                   <- do pacote do Neutrino
  |   |   +-- nomes.txt                  <- opcional (nomes da aba CDVD)
  |   |   +-- CAPAS\
  |   |   |   +-- PS2\                   <- capas, logos e discos de PS2
  |   |   |   +-- PS1\                   <- capas, logos e discos de PS1
  |   |   |   +-- SERIAIS\               <- discos pelo serial (aba CDVD)
  |   |   +-- MEMORY CARD\               <- memory cards virtuais (.mcv)
  |   |
  |   +-- EXTRAS\                        <- Retro Arcade
  |       +-- A7F3C1\                    <- menu e nucleos protegidos
  |       |   +-- 9B14.SYS  
  |       |   +-- 8D2A.SYS  
  |       |   +-- C47E.SYS  
  |       |   +-- 1F90.SYS  
  |       |   +-- B6D3.SYS  
  |       |   +-- 5E08.SYS  
  |       +-- CPS1\   rominfo.cps1  zipname.cps1  ROMS\  CAPAS\  NVRAM\
  |       +-- CPS2\   rominfo.cps2  zipname.cps2  ROMS\  CACHE\  CAPAS\  NVRAM\
  |       +-- MVS\    rominfo.mvs   zipname.mvs   ROMS\  CACHE\  CAPAS\  NVRAM\  MEMCARD\
  |       +-- PCE\    ROMS\
  |       +-- NEOGEO-CD\
  |
  +-- EMBER\                             <- PS1: fica na RAIZ, fora do RETROVOLT
  |   +-- ember.elf
  |   +-- bios.bin                       <- BIOS do seu console
  |   +-- games\
  |       +-- Alundra\                   <- uma pasta por jogo
  |       |   +-- Alundra.cue
  |       |   +-- Alundra.bin
  |       +-- Final Fantasy VII\         <- varios discos: todos na mesma pasta
  |           +-- Final Fantasy VII (Disc 1).cue + .bin
  |           +-- Final Fantasy VII (Disc 2).cue + .bin
  |           +-- Final Fantasy VII (Disc 3).cue + .bin
  |
  +-- (ISOs de PS2)                      <- em qualquer pasta, ate 4 niveis
      +-- DVD\Jogo.iso                      abaixo da raiz. Ex.: DVD\, CD\,
      +-- JOGOS\Jogo.iso                    JOGOS\, JOGOS\PS2\Luta\ ...
      +-- Jogo.iso

  NO MEMORY CARD DO SLOT 1 (o loader cria sozinho):
    mc0:RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\HDUI-*.CFG
      HDUI-LANG.CFG    idioma (PT ou EN)
      HDUI-FAVS.CFG    favoritos
      HDUI-RENAME.CFG  nomes trocados
      HDUI-MODES.CFG   modos de compatibilidade
      HDUI-MCV.CFG     jogos com memory card virtual
      HDUI-LAST.CFG    ultimo jogo (voltar onde parou)
      HDUI-NET.CFG     IP do PS2 na rede
      HDUI-BG.CFG      ordem do fundo


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 4. INSTALACAO, PASSO A PASSO
----------------------------------------------------------------------

 PASSO 1 - A SUITE
   1. Ligue o HD (ou pendrive) no PC.
   2. Descompacte o Vxx_retrovolt_full.zip na RAIZ dele.
      Fica G:\RETROVOLT\... (G: = a letra do seu HD/pendrive).
   3. Ja tem uma pasta RETROVOLT? Descompacte POR CIMA. O pacote so
      troca os programas; seus jogos, capas, saves e memory cards
      virtuais continuam la.

 PASSO 2 - O NEUTRINO (jogos de PS2)
   1. Baixe o pacote mais novo do Neutrino (projeto oficial no GitHub).
   2. Copie para G:\RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\ os TRES itens juntos:
        neutrino.elf   +   pasta config\   +   pasta modules\
   3. Nunca misture versoes (neutrino.elf de uma, config/modules de
      outra): da tela preta. Ao atualizar, troque os tres de uma vez.
   4. Onde o loader procura o Neutrino, nesta ordem:
        1) pendrive: RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\neutrino.elf
        2) pendrive, na raiz: neutrino.elf
        3) HD: RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\neutrino.elf
        4) memory card: mc0:RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\neutrino.elf
      Use UMA copia so. Com duas, vale a primeira da lista (e as
      configuracoes da outra sao ignoradas).

 PASSO 3 - O EMBER (jogos de PS1)
   1. Crie a pasta EMBER na RAIZ do HD ou do pendrive (fora do RETROVOLT).
   2. Coloque nela o ember.elf (Beta 2 ou mais novo) e a bios.bin do
      seu proprio console.
   3. Dentro dela, crie a pasta games\ e uma pasta para cada jogo, com o
      .cue e o .bin dentro. Jogo de varios discos: todos os .cue/.bin na
      mesma pasta.
   4. O PS1 so funciona pelo HD ou pelo pendrive (ainda nao pelo MX4SIO
      nem pelo MMCE).

 PASSO 4 - OS JOGOS DE PS2
   1. Copie as ISOs para o HD/pendrive, em qualquer pasta ate 4 niveis
      abaixo da raiz (ex.: DVD\, CD\, JOGOS\).
   2. Nao coloque ISOs dentro de RETROVOLT, EMBER ou APPS: essas pastas
      nao sao lidas na busca.
   3. Pendrive em FAT32: ISO de 4 GB ou mais nao cabe. Use exFAT.

 PASSO 5 - OS JOGOS DO RETRO ARCADE
   CPS1 / CPS2 / MVS:
     - ROMs (.zip do MAME) em EXTRAS\CPS1\ROMS, CPS2\ROMS e MVS\ROMS.
     - O rominfo e o zipname de cada sistema ficam na pasta do sistema
       (EXTRAS\CPS1\rominfo.cps1, zipname.cps1 ...). Sem eles a aba nao
       aparece.
     - CPS2: cada jogo precisa do CACHE, gerado no PC a partir do .zip
       (romcnv_cps2.exe / gerar_caches.bat), em EXTRAS\CPS2\CACHE.
     - MVS: a BIOS neogeo.zip vai em EXTRAS\MVS\ROMS. Jogos grandes
       tambem usam cache em EXTRAS\MVS\CACHE.
     - CPS2 e Neo-Geo pesados: use o HD interno (exFAT). No pendrive e
       no MX4SIO podem engasgar.
   PC ENGINE:
     - HuCard (.pce) ou ISO (.cue + .bin) em EXTRAS\PCE\ROMS, ou o CD
       original no leitor.
   NEO GEO CD:
     - Coloque o CD (original ou gravado) no leitor do PS2. A BIOS ja
       vem dentro do nucleo. A pasta EXTRAS\NEOGEO-CD precisa existir.

 PASSO 6 - O PROGRAMA DE WINDOWS (opcional)
   Abra o RetroVoltSuite.exe (nao precisa instalar).
   - Idioma: na 1a vez ele pergunta "Portugues (PT-BR) / English (ENG)".
     Trocar depois: caixa de idioma no canto de cima, a direita (o
     programa reabre no idioma novo). Fica gravado no RetroVoltSuite.ini.
   - Parou o mouse em cima de um botao ou opcao: aparece um balao
     explicando o que ele faz.
   - Aba "Capas e MCV":
       1. "Escolher unidade dos jogos...": escolha a unidade (HD/pendrive)
          onde estao os jogos. O programa varre TUDO sozinho (raiz, CD,
          DVD, EMBER\games...). Nessa unidade ele tambem cria a estrutura
          RETROVOLT que faltar e, se as pastas da suite estiverem em
          minusculo (retrovolt, fastloader, capas...), passa para
          MAIUSCULO. Nunca cria CD nem DVD.
       2. Capa, logo e disco que voce copiou a mao para
          RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\CAPAS\PS2 (ou PS1) com o nome do jogo
          (JOGO.PNG, JOGO_LOGO.PNG, JOGO_ICO.PNG) contam como "Ja existe no
          dispositivo" na proxima leitura - o jogo deixa de ficar vermelho.
       3. "Escolher unidade de destino...": o HD/pendrive do PS2. O destino
          comeca SEMPRE vazio: voce decide. O programa cria o que faltar
          em RETROVOLT (e so em RETROVOLT; nunca no disco do Windows).
       4. "Baixar e gerar capas": baixa capa, logo e disco de cada jogo.
          O que ja existe so e trocado com "Sobrescrever capas que ja
          existem" ligado.
       5. Coluna MCV + "Criar MCV dos jogos marcados": cria memory cards
          virtuais de 8 MB, ja formatados.
   - Aba "Retroarcade": capas dos jogos de CPS1, CPS2, MVS e PC Engine.
   - Aba "Rede": servidor para jogar ISOs do PC pelo cabo de rede.
   - Protecao dos nucleos: se o programa achar .ELF soltos da suite
     (RETROARCADE.ELF, CPS1.ELF, PCE.ELF...), pergunta se pode troca-los
     pelos .SYS protegidos. Se o .SYS ja existe, mostra os tamanhos e so
     troca se voce confirmar (o padrao e NAO).

 PASSO 7 - O LAUNCHER DO PS2
   No FreeMcBoot / PS2BBL, crie uma entrada apontando para o arquivo:
       RETROVOLT/FASTLOADER/FASTLOADER.ELF
   Ex. no pendrive: mass:/RETROVOLT/FASTLOADER/FASTLOADER.ELF
   Para o HD, use o caminho que o seu launcher usa para o HD exFAT.
   Ou abra pelo wLaunchELF/uLaunchELF navegando ate o arquivo.

 PASSO 8 - PRIMEIRA VEZ NO PS2
   1. Abra o FASTLOADER.ELF.
   2. Aparece o popup "PT-BR / ENG" (precisa de memory card no slot 1).
      Esquerda/direita escolhem, X grava. Nao pergunta mais.
   3. Pronto: tela principal com as abas.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 5. USANDO NO DIA A DIA
----------------------------------------------------------------------

 ABAS (L1 / R1 trocam):
   HD, USB, MX4SIO, MMCE   jogos de PS2 de cada aparelho
   PS1                     jogos de PS1 (pergunta HD ou USB)
   CDVD                    o disco que esta no leitor
   REDE (NETW em ingles)   jogos de PS2 do PC pelo cabo
   FILES                   gerenciador de arquivos

 IMPORTANTE: nenhuma aba le sozinha. Entre na aba e aperte X para
 carregar. SELECT le de novo (depois de copiar jogos novos).

 BOTOES NAS LISTAS:
   X               carrega a lista / inicia o jogo (pergunta antes)
   Triangulo       renomear (so o nome mostrado)
   Quadrado        modos de compatibilidade do Neutrino
   Circulo         sair para o menu do PS2
   Esquerda        adiciona aos favoritos (ate 10)
   L2 / R2         pagina anterior / proxima
   SELECT          atualizar a lista
   START           Extras
   START + SELECT  favoritos
   R3              troca MX4SIO <-> MMCE (so nas abas deles)

 EXTRAS (START):
   Desligar console / Reset / Creditos / Retro Arcade / Idioma

 INICIAR UM JOGO DE PS2:
   1. Escolha o jogo e aperte X.
   2. No popup, a linha MEMORY CARD: esquerda/direita escolhem
        FISICO (REAL)  = o cartao de verdade do slot 1
        VIRTUAL        = o arquivo .mcv daquele jogo
        CRIAR VIRTUAL  = cria o .mcv na hora e ja inicia
   3. X inicia.

 RETRO ARCADE:
   1. START > Extras > Retro Arcade.
   2. L1/R1 trocam o sistema (CPS1, CPS2, MVS, PC Engine, Neo Geo CD).
   3. X carrega a lista; X no jogo pergunta e inicia.
   4. Popup de iniciar: esquerda/direita escolhem 240p / 480i / 480p.
   5. Ao sair do jogo, volta sozinho ao Retro Arcade ("Voltando ao
      Retro Arcade"), no mesmo jogo.
   6. Voltar ao FastLoader: START no Retro Arcade > Voltar ao FastLoader.

 TROCAR O IDIOMA:
   START > Extras > Idioma. Vale para o FastLoader e o Retro Arcade.
   Para ver o popup da primeira vez de novo: apague
   mc0:RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\HDUI-LANG.CFG.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 6. MEMORY CARD VIRTUAL (MCV)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  - Um arquivo de 8 MB que o jogo enxerga como o memory card do slot 1.
  - Fica em RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\MEMORY CARD\ do MESMO aparelho do jogo.
  - Vale para HD, pendrive e MX4SIO. Nao vale para MMCE, rede, PS1 e
    disco no leitor.
  - Nome: o que vem antes do " - " no nome da ISO (ou os 30 primeiros
    caracteres). Ex.: "Phantom Brave - USA.iso" -> "Phantom Brave.mcv".
  - No pendrive, salvar demora (minutos). Nao desligue durante o save.
  - "MEMORY CARD: FISICO (NOME LONGO)": o caminho do jogo e comprido
    demais para o limite do console. Encurte o nome da ISO ou tire o
    jogo de subpastas.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 7. JOGAR PELA REDE (OPCIONAL)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. PS2 e PC no mesmo roteador (o PS2 por cabo). PS2 fat precisa do
     adaptador de rede.
  2. No PC: RetroVoltSuite.exe > aba Rede > escolha a pasta dos jogos >
     "Liberar no Firewall do Windows..." (so na 1a vez) > "Iniciar
     servidor".
  3. No PS2: aba REDE > X > acerte o IP do PS2 (os 3 primeiros numeros
     iguais aos do PC, o ultimo diferente) > X conecta.
  4. Nao feche o programa nem tire o cabo com o jogo rodando.
  5. Jogo da rede salva no memory card de verdade (sem MCV).


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 8. ATUALIZAR A SUITE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. Baixe o Vxx_retrovolt_full.zip mais novo.
  2. Descompacte na raiz do HD/pendrive, POR CIMA da pasta RETROVOLT.
  3. So isso. Jogos, capas, saves e memory cards virtuais ficam.
  Pode apagar, se ainda existirem:
    - a pasta antiga RETROVOLT\RETROARCADE\;
    - qualquer .ELF dentro de RETROVOLT\EXTRAS (CPS1.ELF, PCE.ELF,
      NEOGEOCD.ELF, RETROARCADE.ELF, _MVS.ELF...);
    - copias antigas do FastLoader (v2.0.8.ELF, v2.0.9.ELF...).
  NAO apague nem renomeie os .SYS de RETROVOLT\EXTRAS\A7F3C1.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 9. PROBLEMAS COMUNS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  Lista vazia
    -> Aperte X na aba (nenhuma aba le sozinha). "Nenhum ... detectado"
       = o aparelho nao respondeu (confira exFAT/FAT32). "Nenhuma ISO
       encontrada" = nao ha ISO nas pastas lidas.

  "NEUTRINO NAO ENCONTRADO"
    -> Falta a pasta do Neutrino em RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\ (pendrive, HD
       ou memory card). Copie neutrino.elf + config + modules.

  Jogo de PS2 trava / tela preta
    -> Teste os modos (Quadrado). Confira se o Neutrino esta completo e
       todo da mesma versao.

  "RETRO ARCADE NAO ENCONTRADO"
    -> Falta RETROVOLT\EXTRAS\A7F3C1\9B14.SYS. Copie o pacote de novo.

  "RETRO ARCADE DANIFICADO" ou nucleo "danificado"
    -> Um .SYS foi alterado ou copiado pela metade. Copie a pasta
       RETROVOLT\EXTRAS\A7F3C1 de novo, do pacote.

  Retro Arcade: "Pasta ... nao encontrada" ou lista vazia
    -> CPS1/CPS2/MVS: falta a pasta do sistema ou o rominfo dentro dela.
       PC Engine / Neo Geo CD: falta a pasta (PCE / NEOGEO-CD) ou o .SYS.

  CPS2: "Jogo sem cache"
    -> Gere o cache do jogo no PC e copie para EXTRAS\CPS2\CACHE.

  MVS: "Falta a BIOS"
    -> Coloque o neogeo.zip em EXTRAS\MVS\ROMS.

  PS1: "EMBER.ELF NAO ENCONTRADO"
    -> Falta EMBER\ember.elf na raiz do aparelho escolhido.

  MX4SIO ou MMCE nao aparece
    -> Os dois nao funcionam juntos. Na aba do outro, aperte R3.

  Sem capa
    -> A capa tem que estar em RETROVOLT\FASTLOADER\CAPAS\PS2 (ou PS1)
       no MESMO aparelho do jogo. Use o RetroVoltSuite.exe.

  Qual versao eu tenho?
    -> START > Creditos: "Retro Volt Suite - FastLoader V2.1.1 - data".


----------------------------------------------------------------------
 Retro Volt Suite - CRIADO POR RETROVOLT - LEONARDO TORRES
======================================================================

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.19
xareleases.body:
- RA mark in the game list can go after the name (Display Settings), so the list stays alphabetical
- Smaller RA mark on the cover, without the frame
- Linux ARM64 client for the Raspberry Pi: xerabora-linux-aarch64

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.18
xareleases.body:
## Fixed

- Games with a large achievement set could launch with no telemetry: the list of memory addresses arrived on the console damaged, and the console dropped it. Found on Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks, which watches 2679 addresses. After the fix the game streams from the first second and the achievements unlock on hardware.
- The hardcore flag read from the Web API was wrong whenever an unlock had both dates, which a hardcore unlock always has.

## Added

- The rich presence line the game is sending, on the CONSOLE panel.
- UNLOCK ON THE TV on SETTINGS: off keeps every unlock on the page and sends nothing to the console, for games whose picture the flash breaks. Saved between runs.
- LIVE: ACHIEVEMENTS and LEADERBOARDS as two sub-tabs. ACHIEVEMENTS as the list, each row with its median unlock time, or as GRID, the badges alone as on the site. An unlocked badge wears a ring for the mode it was earned in: blue softcore, gold hardcore, half and half when both. GAME has the same LIST / GRID choice.

## Removed

- The cheat engine. OPL-RA no longer carries PS2RD, reads no `CHT/` files and has no cheat menu; stock OPL is for play with cheats.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.17...v0.1.0-alpha.18

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.17
xareleases.body:
## Fixed

- Mode 6 (in-game reset off) no longer stops the achievements. The per-frame snapshot ran only from the IGR's VBLANK handler, so a game set to Mode 6 sent nothing to the PC. The loader now installs a handler with the snapshot alone in that mode: no IGR thread, no padOpen patch, no syscall hooks. Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus, which takes the IGR for tampering and hides its collectibles, runs clean under Mode 6 with its achievements (#15). Checked on hardware from an SMB share.

## Known limits

- RESET CONSOLE from the client needs the IGR, so it does nothing under Mode 6.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.16...v0.1.0-alpha.17

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.16
xareleases.body:
## Added

- PS1 games through POPStarter. A `.VCD` in `POPS/` on a USB stick is listed with the PS2 games, marked PS1, and runs in Sony's PS1 emulator with the game's PS1 achievement set. Check it once with "RA: check game support", launch, play: the console reads the PS1 memory from the IOP and streams it as for a PS2 game. What goes in `POPS/` and what is not covered: [USAGE, "PS1 games through POPStarter"](https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md#ps1-games-through-popstarter).
- Settings → "PS1 USB drive is exFAT". POPStarter's own driver reads FAT32 only; with this on, OPL puts the BDMAssault `usbexfat` pair on the memory card before the launch and takes it off when the setting is off.

## Known limits

- PS1 is tested from USB, FAT32 and exFAT. MX4SIO, iLink and an exFAT HDD get their driver pair the same way but were not run here. Not covered: PS1 from an MMCE device, an APA HDD or a share. No gold flash under POPS, the unlock shows on the client's page. The telemetry starts 25 seconds after the launch.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.15...v0.1.0-alpha.16

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.15
xareleases.body:
## Added

- Games from an SD card in an MMCE device (SD2PSX, MemCard PRO2 and others) in the memory card slot. Turn it on in OPL under Settings → MMCE Settings; the games get their own page, and "RA: check game support" and the achievements work as on USB. Built on the MMCE team's OPL work.
- QUIT sits in the header on every screen. On a phone it had no button at all: the footer it lived in is hidden on narrow screens.
- An ABOUT section at the bottom of SETTINGS: the version you run, a note when a newer release is out, and links to the troubleshooting guide, the issue tracker, Discord and the project page.
- [Before you report a problem](https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/blob/main/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md): how to reset everything to a known state and what to collect before opening an issue.

## Fixed

- Android: the battery optimisation prompt came back neither after "Later" nor after a refusal. Now it says where to allow it and asks again at the next start, unless you choose "Don't show again". By MrRexD.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.14...v0.1.0-alpha.15

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.14
xareleases.body:
## Added

- An Android app. The phone runs the whole client, no PC needed: the console finds it on the Wi-Fi the way it finds a PC, and each unlock shows up as a notification. Install `xerabora-android.apk` from this release (Android 8.0 or later). Made by [MrRexD](https://github.com/oMrRexD).
- A Discord server for the project: https://discord.gg/JZVNPF7cS2

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-ManoAlpha.13...v0.1.0-alpha.14

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-ManoAlpha.13
xareleases.body:
## Fixed

- Some games hung about ten seconds after start, as soon as the first memory snapshot was taken. Their achievement sets read memory at addresses the console could not read in one go. Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is one of them. Those reads work now.
- A snapshot that arrived while the previous one was still being sent could be lost.
- A watch list with a broken entry is refused instead of shifting every value after it.
- Games on an SD card in the memory card slot (MX4SIO) did not boot: the driver they need now travels with the game.

## Added

- Pointer chains that carry an address mask are followed. Scooby-Doo! and the Spooky Swamp goes from 10 supported chains to all 71.
- RESET CONSOLE on the LIVE page sends the console back to the loader menu, no button combo needed. Where it lands is OPL's IGR Path setting: point it at a copy of the ELF on the memory card to come back to OPL+RA.
- The release build no longer writes hash logs to the share; the debug build keeps them.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.12...v0.1.0-ManoAlpha.13

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.12
xareleases.body:
## Improved

- The client's page is redrawn. A plain theme in place of the pixel one, a layout that fits a phone, and a look that follows the source: while the console streams the page turns gold and the cover spins as a disc that stumbles on lost packets; while following an emulator it turns blue.
- Library cards and the game head show two progress bars, softcore and hardcore, with the award in the corner of the cover.
- An achievement can be hidden from UP NEXT. The next one by median takes its slot, and "N hidden · SHOW ALL" brings them back.
- The page is now written in pieces under `client/ui/src` on Preact, and `tools/build-page.py` assembles, embeds and rebuilds the demo.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.11...v0.1.0-alpha.12

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.11
xareleases.body:
- Big achievement sets are supported: the watch list is split into chunks, so a set that did not fit in one packet now reaches the console.
- The console shows why a set was refused (unknown game, set too big, server down) instead of a generic message, and waits longer for the answer.
- A dump the set does not match is reported as the wrong dump.
- Added a survey mode in the client: it counts what a set needs before you play it.

- The image check failed when the client remembered another game from an earlier session.
- A game launched from a USB stick with a stored watch list sent no telemetry: the network adapter was not powered.
- Loading a set blocked the client for seconds and the console gave up waiting. Loading now runs in the background.
- On Windows the client could start a second copy of itself.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.10...v0.1.0-alpha.11

xareleases.name: v0.1.0-alpha.10
xareleases.body:
## Improved

- Achievements that read through a pointer now unlock. The console follows the pointer while the game runs; sets that were largely out of reach are playable.

## Fixed

- The live leaderboard list no longer hangs on screen with its last value after the console goes away.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hacan359/xerabora/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.9...v0.1.0-alpha.10

rireleases.name: Rip it: RIPPS2 v1.1.0 beta (build 110)
rireleases.body:
## Rip it: RIPPS2 v1.1.0 beta (build 110) **[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.1.0-beta/RIPPS2.elf)** (one file, about 3 MB) and put it in place of your old one. Your settings stay where they were. **[RIPPS2-languages.zip](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.1.0-beta/RIPPS2-languages.zip)** puts RIPPS2 in your language (copy its `LNG` folder to the top of a USB drive, the HDD's OPL partition or an MMCE card, then Settings > Display Settings > Language). The **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** is still edition 108; RIPGRID and RIPFLOW are built in.

### Every source lists at once - **Every source shows its last list the moment it answers.** Build 109 kept an MMCE card's game list on the card; now MMCE, USB, the internal exFAT HDD, MX4SIO, iLink and SMB all keep `RIPPS2.LST` beside their CD and DVD folders. The drive is read again the next time you are idle on Storage, and the list follows whatever changed. With Write Operations Off no list is written. - **The APA HDD's own list cache is on** (Cache Game List (HDD APA), switched on once for older settings), and the APA table is read again the next time you are idle, so a game installed from a PC still appears without a refresh. - **MX4SIO pauses for the pads while it is read**, as MMCE does: both share the controllers' bus. ### Save Settings To, every drive - **Settings > General > Save Settings To** offers USB Drive, MX4SIO, iLink and MMCE as well as Memory Card, Internal HDD and Custom Path, each with its own hint. A drive is saved by its type (`usb0:/RIPPS2`, `mx4sio0:/RIPPS2`, `ilink0:/RIPPS2`, `mmce0:/RIPPS2`) with its RIPPS2 folder made for it, so at boot only that drive's driver loads. A drive that is not connected says so and nothing changes. - SMB and UDPBD cannot hold the settings: reaching them needs the settings. ### Info page - **A game reached with the d-pad on the info page shows its size** (every game after the first read 0 MiB). ### Underneath - The new words in all 33 languages. **[Full changelog](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)** | **[Watch the v1.1.0 reel](https://youtu.be/Q8ZLd6ArV8s)** | **[Talk about it on psx-place](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/)** | [RIPPCSX2](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPCSX2/releases/latest) for seeing a theme in true 720p and 1080i Beta: keep your usual loader close by, and tell us what breaks in [the psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or [an issue](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/issues). This one wants big libraries on real drives above all: how fast does your list show on the second boot, and do settings saved to a USB drive, MX4SIO, iLink or MMCE come back after a power cycle?

rireleases.name: Rip it: RIPPS2 v1.0.9 beta (builds 108 and 109)
rireleases.body:
## Rip it: RIPPS2 v1.0.9 beta (builds 108 and 109) **[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.0.9-beta/RIPPS2.elf)** (one file, about 3 MB) and put it in place of your old one. Your settings stay where they were. **[RIPPS2-languages.zip](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.0.9-beta/RIPPS2-languages.zip)** puts RIPPS2 in your language (copy its `LNG` folder to the top of a USB drive, the HDD's OPL partition or an MMCE card, then Settings > Display Settings > Language). The **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** has a new edition (v108: Adapt and Adapt Rx show every screenshot): replace your Adapt folders. RIPGRID and RIPFLOW are built in.

### Build 109: from testers' reports - **A big MMCE library lists at once.** The card keeps RIPPS2's last list of its games (`RIPPS2.LST`, beside its CD and DVD folders): at boot the games show from it straight away, then the card is read again in the background and the list follows whatever changed. A tester's 180 games took about 5 minutes to list on every boot, with nothing to press until then. - **The pads keep working while an MMCE card is read.** The card shares its bus with the controllers; the scan now pauses after each game, and a frame after each disc it has to open. - **Settings > General > Save Settings To:** Memory Card (RIPPS2's own save, as before), **Internal HDD** (a RIPPS2 folder on the internal exFAT HDD, else the APA HDD's OPL partition; settings are read from there first) or Custom Path (the Custom Settings Path row shows only for this one). Every choice has its own hint; with no internal HDD it says so and changes nothing. - **A settings page's title stands clear of the line under it** (it sat on the line, which cut its descenders). - **Hotfix (10/21, still build 109):** Internal HDD is saved by the drive's type (`ata0:/RIPPS2`), not its mass slot, so a USB stick can't take its place and the boot loads only the HDD's driver. If you chose Internal HDD on the first v1.0.9 ELF, choose it again and Save Changes. ### Build 108: RIPSHOT, screenshots from the in-game menu - **SCREENSHOT is the in-game menu's third choice** (L1+L2+R1+R2+SELECT+START). It takes **the exact frame that was up when the menu opened**, with no menu in it. - **ART, MEDIA or BOTH:** ART is the game's screenshot art for your themes (250 x 188, `_SCR`, `_SCR2`, `_SCR3`...), MEDIA a full-size PNG in a folder named for the game. Each choice shows the file it becomes, its size, the drive and the shots left. **SAVE** fades the menu off, then **KEEP** or **DELETE**. - **6 shots a game** wait on its roll in `MEDIA/RIPSHOT` until developed into 8-bit PNGs. **Develop Shots: Manual** (the default) does it from Memory Files (open `MEDIA/RIPSHOT`: VIEW a shot, ACTIONS to develop it); **Auto** does it in the background once you are back in RIPPS2. - **Themes show every shot** with the new `SCRn` key: RIPPS2's info page slideshow, RIPGRID, RIPFLOW, Adapt and Adapt Rx use it, so a shot appears as soon as it is developed ([THEME_KEYS.md](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/blob/main/docs/THEME_KEYS.md)). - For now: games on USB, the internal exFAT HDD, MX4SIO and iLink. The APA HDD, MMCE, SMB and discs say NOT FOR THIS GAME. ### The in-game menu - **Silent, and RESUME gives back the exact frame:** the game's sound holds still while the menu is open and goes on where it was, so nothing skips, loops or drifts out of sync. - **On by default**, no longer experimental (a config from an older build gets it switched on once). **Settings > General > In-Game Menu** is its own page: In-Game Menu, RIPSHOT and Develop Shots, every choice with its own hint. A setting another one switches off now reads dimmed on every settings page. - Fixed in the lab: a game that sets a picture taller than the TV put the menu off screen; GSM's data breakpoint froze the menu. ### Found while making the reel - **The info page no longer blinks** when a device rescan rebuilds the game list under it: it knows a game by its id and title, not by its row. - **Shots developed while RIPPS2 runs show at once**, and a developed PNG is checked on the drive and written again if it did not hold. ### Underneath - **Games launch in PCSX2 with its host filesystem on** (the launch used to hang there). - The new words in all 33 languages. **[Full changelog](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)** | **[Watch the beta reel](https://youtu.be/LPjdK_E1jjM)** | **[Talk about it on psx-place](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/)** | [RIPPCSX2](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPCSX2/releases/latest) for seeing a theme in true 720p and 1080i Beta: keep your usual loader close by, and tell us what breaks in [the psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or [an issue](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/issues). This one wants real consoles above all: an MMCE with a big library, settings on an internal HDD after a power cycle, and RIPSHOT on USB, MX4SIO, iLink and the HDD in 480p, 1080i and PAL games.

rireleases.body:
## Rip it: RIPPS2 v1.0.7 beta (build 107) **[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.0.7-beta/RIPPS2.elf)** (one file, about 3 MB) and put it in place of your old one. Your settings stay in your memory card's RIPPS2 save. New: **[RIPPS2-languages.zip](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.0.7-beta/RIPPS2-languages.zip)** puts RIPPS2 in your language (copy its `LNG` folder to the top of a USB drive, the HDD's OPL partition or an MMCE card, then Settings > Display Settings > Language). The **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** has a new edition (v107: Adapt and Adapt Rx with the new list keys): replace your Adapt folders. RIPGRID and RIPFLOW are built in.

### RIPDISC: your discs, kept (build 105) - **Launch Disc rips the disc in the drive.** After 4.2 seconds a glass panel fades in: RIPDISC. Hold **SELECT** for 4.2 seconds (a ring fills round it) and the confirm step says what the disc is, its size, **how long it should take** and where it goes. Confirm, then **START**. Cancelling asks first, then removes everything written. - **PS2 games** become an ISO in the drive's DVD or CD folder, in your games list. Over 4 GB on a drive that may be FAT32 (USB, MX4SIO, iLink), Open PS2 Loader's 1 GB parts with ul.cfg instead; the internal exFAT HDD keeps one ISO. Left / Right picks the drive. Dual-layer DVDs and ESR discs too. - **PS1 games** become a BIN and CUE in `EMBER/games//`, for Ember. - **Audio CDs and DVD videos** go to your files: Memory Files opens on a new **MEDIA** folder beside AUDIO, the clipboard reading **RIPPED**; PASTE anywhere rips it there. A CD lands as WAVs and the keyboard asks for the folder's name; a DVD you made as its VIDEO_TS files (bought films are copy protected and the drive will not read them). - **How long, up front.** The PS2's USB is USB 1.1, about 1 MB a second: a 4 GB DVD to a stick is over an hour, to the internal exFAT HDD far less. After your first rip RIPPS2 remembers the speed your console really got and the next estimate is its own. - **AUDIO takes any .ogg or .wav as music** by its own name (a ripped track needs no `bgm_04`), and AUDIO and MEDIA get a README.txt explaining themselves. - Checked in the lab: a 1.2 GB PS2 game ripped from PCSX2's drive to an exFAT HDD came out byte for byte the source. ### RIPPS2 in your language (build 104) - **33 languages read all of RIPPS2**, not only Open PS2 Loader's settings: French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese (both), Dutch, Danish, Swedish, Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Romanian, Croatian, Serbian, Albanian, Galician, Greek, Russian, Bulgarian, Turkish, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Filipino, Cebuano, Lao, Chinese (both), Japanese, Korean, Ryukyuan, **Arabic and Persian right to left with their letters joined**. - Every script draws: a language that needs other letters has its font in the pack (Lao in Noto Sans Lao, Arabic and Persian in DejaVu Sans), Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Lao lines break where they should, and long words fit (a hint row a translation overfills reads a size smaller). ### In game, Storage and Memory Files (builds 106 and 107) - **POWER OFF** is the in-game menu's last choice: the second press turns the PS2 off right there (a disc game keeps the power button). - **The star sits at the start of the row**, titles lined up. **Settings > Game Sources > Starred Games Star**: Theme, Left, Right or Hidden. A theme's row icon moves to the row's end out of its way. - **SEARCH FILES** replaces MC EXPLOIT INSTALLER in Memory Files' settings grid: any file or folder by name on every started drive, opened in the tree where it is. - **New theme keys** for the games list: `star`, `star_image`, `highlight` (bar, line, none), `decorator_all`, `decorator_ps2` / `_ps1` / `_app` ([THEME_KEYS.md](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/blob/main/docs/THEME_KEYS.md)). ### Underneath (build 103) - **RiptOPL brought up to 10/18/2026** (548 upstream commits): in-game reset input a busy game can no longer starve, settings saves that survive a failed write, safer IOP resets and VMCs, RetroAchievements fixes, CFG Titles in the lists, a CJK title fallback font, per-game parental locks. RIPPS2's own look and features stay as they were. - **The version line tells the truth:** About, Settings and the boot screen show `RIPPS2 v1.0.7-beta (build 107) on RiptOPL v1.2.0-Beta-4032-3cd7f89`. **[Full changelog](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)** | **[Watch the beta reel](https://youtu.be/LPjdK_E1jjM)** | **[Talk about it on psx-place](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/)** | [RIPPCSX2](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPCSX2/releases/latest) for seeing a theme in true 720p and 1080i Beta: keep your usual loader close by, and tell us what breaks in [the psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or [an issue](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/issues). RIPDISC wants real drives above all: big DVDs, dual-layer games, audio CDs and PS1 discs, and how long they took on your console. POWER OFF in the in-game menu could not be shown in the emulator: tell us how it goes on hardware.

rireleases.name: Kill it: RIPPS2 v1.0.2 beta (build 102)
rireleases.body:
## Kill it: RIPPS2 v1.0.2 beta (build 102) **[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.0.2-beta/RIPPS2.elf)** (one file, about 3 MB) and put it in place of your old one. The **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** has a new edition (v102: Adapt and Adapt Rx): replace your Adapt folders. RIPGRID and RIPFLOW are built in.

### Sound - **No more beeping while a load is stuck.** When the music's read stalled (a drive coming back after an in-game reset, a busy card, the ripped menu music read from a drive), the PS2's sound driver ran out and played its last tenth of a second over and over. The music now fills the gap with silence until its next piece arrives. - **Switching away from stuck music no longer freezes the menu** for seconds while the read finishes. - **The console boot sound starts with the towers**, not the moment it has loaded. - **Adapt plays your ripped sounds** (a new theme key, `sounds=audio`), even copied over an older Adapt that shipped sounds of its own. ### Every theme - **No info page switches the source.** Left, Right, Up and Down go through the games on every theme. - **Colors and More edits every theme's colours.** On RIPGRID and themes from a drive the colour rows were greyed out and the cursor skipped them. Now they change that theme's own colours, kept for it alone; Reset gives its own back. - **Apps show a square PS1 case by default.** Triangle on an app: **Case Shape** PS1, PS2 or Theme, kept for that app. - **Reflections and cased covers fade with their page**, long text slides smoothly a pixel at a time, and **About and STATUS read in RIPPS2's own type** on every theme, About's credits wrapping evenly inside the panel. ### Memory Files - **A game started from the file browser starts its drive's games itself.** A drive opened only with START DRIVES could not launch a game until it was opened once in Storage. ### Themes - **RIPGRID:** Standard glyphs (L3 and R3 included); the grid raised so the space above and below it match; the info page lined up, its logo just above the text; the CD player and file tree like RIPFLOW's, Launch Disc and Memory Files like RIPPS2's. - **RIPFLOW:** White glyphs, hints in RIPPS2 Sleek Case, badges and stars at their true shapes in one row. - **Adapt and Adapt Rx (edition 102):** the disc and case at real-life proportions (a 120 mm disc over a 135 x 190 mm case), lined up with the list's box; logos just above the info box (`valign=bottom`); readable hints on every page; the apps page under the category bar with a square case. **[Full changelog](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)** | **[Watch the beta reel](https://youtu.be/LPjdK_E1jjM)** | **[Talk about it on psx-place](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/)** | [RIPPCSX2](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPCSX2/releases/latest) for seeing a theme in true 720p and 1080i Beta: keep your usual loader close by, and tell us what breaks in [the psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or [an issue](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/issues). The sound fixes especially want ears on a real console.

rireleases.name: Kill it: RIPPS2 v1.0.1 beta (build 101)
rireleases.body:
## Kill it: RIPPS2 v1.0.1 beta (build 101)

The first beta, fixed up from what turned up on a real PS2.

**[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.0.1-beta/RIPPS2.elf)** (one file, about 3 MB) and put it in place of your old one. Your settings stay in your memory card's RIPPS2 save. The **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** is unchanged (v100: Adapt and Adapt Rx; RIPGRID and RIPFLOW are built in).

### Fixed in build 101
- **Sounds stay where they belong.** Changing the theme (in Interface or by holding SELECT), an IOP reboot, a BIOS rip and the AUDIO folder found late on a drive all load the sounds again. The PS2 keys every voice off and writes the sounds back one by one, which takes seconds when your rips are on a memory card. Until now the menu kept playing through that: cursor and page sounds were asked of a half-loaded set, and a confirm caught by the load waited until it ended and sounded seconds later, outside the menu it came from. Now nothing touches a voice while a load runs. A cursor tick is dropped, and the newest confirm, cancel or page sound plays when the set is in only if it was pressed within the last 0.3 seconds. Every load also forgets which voice earlier sounds took, and turns the voices down before its reset turns them all up.
- **RIPFLOW's info page:** Left and Right go through the games, as on its carousel, and the info page stays. They no longer switch drives there. Other themes keep Left and Right for the drives.

### Also since v1.0.0
- **RIPGRID's info page** draws its rating stars and badges (480P, 16:9, NTSC...) side by side instead of on top of each other. This was the hotfix of 10/12, already in the v1.0.0 download since then.

### For theme makers
**[RIPPCSX2](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPCSX2/releases/latest)** is PCSX2 v2.9.96 with HDTV output. It shows a front end's 720p and 1080i the way a TV does: 16:9, with screenshots and recordings at 1280 x 720 and 1920 x 1080, and 1080i placed where the console puts it. It works for OPL and RiptOPL themes as well as RIPPS2's.

**[Watch the beta reel](https://youtu.be/LPjdK_E1jjM)** | **[Talk about it on psx-place](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/)** | [Changelog](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

Beta: keep your usual loader close by, and tell us what breaks in [the psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or [an issue](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/issues). The sound fix especially wants ears on a real console.

rireleases.name: Kill it: RIPPS2 v1.0.0 beta (build 100)
rireleases.body:
## Kill it: RIPPS2 v1.0.0 beta (build 100)

**RIPPS2 leaves alpha.** A hundred builds in, tested on consoles and in PCSX2, RIPPS2 is a beta: a PS2 front end in one `.elf` that launches your games, plays your discs, manages your memory cards and files, and draws glass towers and orbits behind it all, live on the PS2.

**[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v1.0.0-beta/RIPPS2.elf)** (one file, about 3 MB), and the **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** if you like (Adapt and Adapt Rx; RIPGRID and RIPFLOW are built in). Copy it to a USB stick or memory card and start it from FreeMcBoot, PS2BBL, wLaunchELF or whatever you already use. In PCSX2: **System > Start File**.

**[Watch the beta reel](https://youtu.be/LPjdK_E1jjM)**: 9:45 of RIPPS2 on the beta, every chapter in the description.

**[Talk about it on psx-place](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/)**: the beta's thread, for questions, reports and what you would like next.

### What RIPPS2 is
- **LAUNCH DISC** boots PS2, PS1 and DVD video discs, names the game in the drive before you start it, and plays audio CDs with the towers as a spectrum analyzer.
- **STORAGE** is your library: every drive in one list (USB, HDD, iLink, MX4SIO, MMCE, network), art and an info page whose art crossfades with the screenshots, per-game settings, Starred Games and Recents, and a random pick on L2 + R2.
- **MEMORY FILES** is a full file manager: copy, move and delete across memory cards, USB and HDD; VMC card images open like folders; PSU export and import; a text editor; pictures, AVI video and 3D save icons; games start right from the browser. Square on a card opens **MCKILLA**, the card manager.
- **Themes:** RIPGRID (a cover grid whose cases turn over to their back covers) and RIPFLOW (a cover carousel) built in, Adapt and Adapt Rx in the pack, six color themes, four glyph sets and your own button hints. Make your own with the [theme kit](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes).
- **Everything on board:** Neutrino 1.8.0, POPSTARTER and Ember ride inside the `.elf` and install themselves where your games are. **BIBLE** sets up PS2BBL so the console boots straight into RIPPS2. **SpiritofRA** brings RetroAchievements through xeRAbora on your PC.
- **Sound from your own console:** BIOS Sounds and BIOS Music rip the PS2's own browser sounds and menu music from its BIOS (nothing from any BIOS ships with RIPPS2), and [RIPPS2 Audio Studio](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/tree/main/tools/audio-studio) makes sounds and music from anything on a PC.

### New in build 100
- **Clean sound.** The ripped boot and launch music no longer pop (three instruments were misread as the SPU2's noise), the startling beep after saving settings is gone, every press makes one sound, and nothing sounds without a press: no sound when art loads, none for drive scans.
- **The menu music, ripped on its own:** Audio settings > BIOS Music > RIP writes your console's ambient menu piece (5:31) as a WAV. Its size (15.1 MB) is shown first and you pick the folder: beside RIPPS2, or OPL's AUDIO folder on a drive. The music list now reads OPL's AUDIO folder on every started drive too.
- **RIPPS2's own memory card save,** `mc0:/RIPPS2`: the dead elf's hat ringing its bell, the settings, nothing else (about 55 KB). No more settings shared with another OPL beside the ELF.
- **Memory Files:** replace is a clean erase, copy and check; an ISO or ZSO starts wherever it is; the text editor reads in RIPPS2 Sleek; the 3D icon viewer turns the way you press.
- **Storage:** POPSTARTER from USB remembers your drive's format, cases turn over from the side you push, and the START menu and Settings read in one clear face on every theme.

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Thanks to ripto, nuno6573, zackcage6, eliminator1403, FifthFox and Mr.sus.60 for a hundred builds of testing. RIPPS2 is built on [RiptOPL](https://github.com/NathanNeurotic/Open-PS2-Loader) (Open PS2 Loader), Neutrino, POPSTARTER, Ember and PS2BBL. Beta: keep your usual loader close by, and tell us what breaks in [the psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or [an issue](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/issues).

rireleases.name: Kill it: RIPPS2 build 99 (alpha)
rireleases.body:
## Kill it: RIPPS2 build 99 (alpha)

**Four builds since 95.** The music gets a road of its own (and half of all music, which never played, plays now), Memory Files grows into a real file manager with games, 3D save icons and its own icon on your card, the Grid and Flow catch up with HD screens, and RIPPS2 calls your drives by what they are.

**[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v0.0.99-alpha/RIPPS2.elf)**, and the **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** if you like (Adapt and Adapt Rx, each with its full key glossary; RIPGRID and RIPFLOW are built in).

**[Watch the 60-second Short](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Ov5iA-tMcI8)**: build 99 in under a minute.

### Music
- **Half of all music never played.** The PS2's Vorbis library refuses an Ogg stream whose serial number has its top bit set, and encoders pick that number at random. RIPPS2 fixes it as it reads, and RIPPS2 Audio Studio no longer writes such files.
- **The music no longer waits in line for the drive:** it is read into memory in big pieces (about 16 seconds of music per request instead of a request every few hundred milliseconds), so loading covers cannot starve it. In the lab a pilot tone ran 90 seconds through a button storm without a dropout.

### Memory Files
- **Both memory cards stay after START DRIVES**, named MEMORY CARD 0 and MEMORY CARD 1. Paste asks YES, REPLACE IT / NO, KEEP IT / YES TO ALL; a full card says so before writing; deletes are checked and explained.
- **Games start right here:** ISO or ZSO in a drive's CD or DVD folder, as from Storage (your Loader Core, VMCs, cheats), and CUE or BIN in `EMBER/games/<game>/` with Ember.
- **3D save icons** open textured and animated; **RIP 3D ICON** writes OBJ, MTL and PNG for a PC. **RIPPS2's own card folder** now has an icon (the dead elf's hat ringing its bell) instead of showing as corrupted data.
- Rest on a file for its details, hold to scroll, the text editor keeps files exactly as they were, and the picture viewer stays sharp zoomed in.

### Grid and Flow
- **RIPGRID's 720p freeze is fixed** (a pad command waited on a controller still starting up). Lists always show a full page.
- **Widescreen Grid layout** for 720p, 1080i and widescreen; L2 / R2 turn a whole page; Vignette Other Covers Off / Weak / Full; Background art blur; RIPFLOW tilts and flips like RIPGRID.
- The game's background fades in right behind its cover; the info page fades in as one again.

### Settings and names
- Back lands on the row you came from, settings read in one plain face on every theme, auto start can be Last Used, page buttons L1 / R1 or L2 / R2.
- **Drives are named by what they are:** USB, HDD, iLINK, MX4SIO, not "USB" for every `mass0:`. **STATUS > DRIVES** lists them and what became of MX4SIO.
- **From RiptOPL:** PS1 games flash their real disc ID for Pixel FX / RetroGEM (#869), and a slow-spinning iLink drive is waited for at start.

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Alpha: keep your usual loader close by.

rireleases.name: Kill it: RIPPS2 build 95 (alpha)
rireleases.body:
## Kill it: RIPPS2 build 95 (alpha)

**Hear it, fix it.** A stability build: the sound effects rebuilt so they never go quiet in waves or bring old sounds back, the boot no longer reading a ripped boot sound behind the drives' back, and the bug that broke RIPFLOW (and more) from build 93 found and fixed.

**[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v0.0.95-alpha/RIPPS2.elf)**, and the **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** if you like (unchanged since build 94).

### Sound effects, rebuilt
- **A held cursor no longer goes quiet in waves, and old sounds no longer come back after.** RIPPS2 now knows when every voice has finished and only plays on one that has. In the lab a held cursor went from bursts of six ticks and 0.8 s of silence to a clean tick every 60 ms.
- **No sounds are built in.** They come from your `AUDIO` folder: **Audio Settings > BIOS Sounds > Rip** makes your own console's, and RIPPS2 Audio Studio makes any others. **STATUS > SOUNDS** says how many are loaded and where from, and can rip them for you.
- **Safer at boot:** every sound file is read by the worker that reads the drives (a ripped `boot.adp` used to be read at boot alongside it, which can hang a memory card), and each file is checked before use, so a bad one is skipped instead of stopping anything.
- **Ripped sounds end at silence** (rip again for the new endings), and **Memory Files plays `.adp` files** so you can check them.

### Fixed
- **RIPFLOW works again.** The video player added in build 93 carried its own copies of the C library's string functions, and they replaced the real ones for all of RIPPS2. That broke RIPFLOW's theme, could hang build 93 at boot, and threw off a count on the console. It cannot happen again: the build now fails if it would.
- **MX4SIO** is identified with those same functions, so it may be back too: tell us.
- **JPG pictures open whole** (no more top quarter only), and **game art can be JPG**: old OPL art packs now show their covers on every theme.

### In-Game Menu
- Now marked **experimental**: some games skip their sound or stop if paused in a cutscene. Off (the default) the combo is OPL's trusted IGR, untouched.

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Alpha: keep your usual loader close by.

rireleases.name: Kill it: RIPPS2 build 94 (alpha)
rireleases.body:
## Kill it: RIPPS2 build 94 (alpha)

**Hunt it, watch it, theme it.** Six builds since 88: what every game has left to hunt (on YOUR ACCOUNT and in the in-game menu), pictures and video in Memory Files, a launch disc that pops in or spins, your own button hints and two new glyph sets, every console sound ripped, and RIPgrid built in.

**[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v0.0.94-alpha/RIPPS2.elf)**, and the **[theme pack for build 94](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** (RIPgrid's disc, serials and title are new).

### New in 94: what is left to hunt (Spirit of RA)
- **CHECK GAME SUPPORT brings the whole set home.** With **OPEN TO THE NETWORK** on in xeRAbora's settings, the check also keeps the game's achievements beside its list (`RA/<serial>.ach`): each one's title, points, how it is earned and whether you have it. With it off, the check is as before.
- **Achievements > YOUR ACCOUNT**: each game's card says how many are left. Cross opens **LEFT TO HUNT**, every locked achievement with its points and how to earn it.
- **In-game menu**: ACHIEVEMENTS says how many are left, and confirm opens LEFT TO HUNT in the pause menu, one at a time (Up and Down for the next, Back to the menu). It shows the list from the last check: check again to bring it up to date.

### New in 93: pictures and video in Memory Files
- **PNG and JPG** open full screen, fitted. R2 and L2 zoom, the D-pad moves, the right stick tilts, Triangle fits it again. Any size opens.
- **AVI video** (XviD or DivX, MP3 or MP2 sound) plays full screen. **START pauses**, Back or SELECT stops, nothing else on the pad is taken. The player is RIPPS2's fork of libsmslite (the SMS player's core).

### New in 91 and 92: the launch disc, Flow and Grid
- **As a game launches, its disc comes in** where Please Wait used to be: **Pop In** (RIPgrid) or **Spin** (RIPFLOW), picked in **Interface > Flow and Grid** (was Coverflow Settings), with **Grid Layout**, and **Vignette Other Covers** in place of Dim.
- **RIPgrid is built in** as `<RIPgrid>`. On the Grid a game with no cover shows its serial, and the chosen name sits under the grid.
- **The category bar** looks the same on every theme; themes can stack it down the side or reword it. **Page Transition**: Fade or Flash between categories.
- Fixed: PS Emulation's **USB BDMA Driver** row ("<no values>"), hidden rows leave no gap, the Network page's layout, and copies of **folders** are called folders.

### New in 90: Hints and Glyphs
- **Controller Settings > Hints and Glyphs**: hint layout (row or column), labels or glyphs only or **Badges**, show or hide each hint, your own **Hint Order**, and the **Glyph Set** on every page: the theme's, RIPPS2's, **Standard** (Adapt's) or **White** (Grunge's).

### New in 89: every console sound
- **BIOS Sounds > Rip** now makes the **boot** and **launch** too, from the console's own system music. **RIPPOPS**: missing `POPS.ELF` and `POPS_IOX.PAK` are copied from a `POPS` folder on another drive. Settings pages get a **scroll bar**, and the right stick slides them.

The in-game menu (Settings > General > In-Game Menu) still needs a real console: PCSX2 cannot show it.

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Alpha: keep your usual loader close by.

rireleases.name: Kill it: RIPPS2 build 88 (alpha)
rireleases.body:
## Kill it: RIPPS2 build 88 (alpha)

**Pause it, rip it, back it up.** Five builds since 83: your console's own sounds ripped by RIPPS2 on the console, an in-game menu, a memory card manager, RiptOPL's latest, and a launch report for the PS1 games that will not start on real hardware.

**[Download RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/download/v0.0.88-alpha/RIPPS2.elf)**, and the **[theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest)** if you like (unchanged since build 83).

**[Watch the 60-second Short](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Sqprz22tdtg)**: builds 84 to 88 in under a minute.

### New in 88: your console's own sounds
- **Audio settings > BIOS Sounds > Rip.** RIPPS2 reads the menu sounds from the BIOS of the console it runs on and writes them into your `AUDIO` folder as its sounds: cursor, confirm, cancel, pages in and out, category, messages, disc, error, save, drive in and out, random. Each one is played the way the console plays it (its envelope, its volume, a little of the hall the browser runs under its menus). No PC, no files passed around. It asks first, because files of those names in `AUDIO` are replaced.
- Boot and game launch stay as they are (on the console those are system music, not menu sounds). Consoles from SCPH-30000 on carry the sounds this way; the first models (BIOS 1.00) are told so.
- **Music** plays the track called Menu first when you have not picked one (`bgm_03 Menu.ogg` in a pack that has it).

### New in 87: an in-game menu (turn it on to test)
- **Settings > General > In-Game Menu.** With it on, **L1+L2+R1+R2+SELECT+START** pauses the game under a plain panel instead of leaving it at once: **Resume**, **Achievements** (SpiritofRA for the game you are in: your unlocks and whether tracking is on) and **Exit Game** (your Exit To path: RIPPS2, the boot lock's loader or the browser; it takes a second press).
- For games RIPPS2 starts with its own loader. Neutrino games keep the old combo for now. PCSX2 cannot show the menu (it has no data breakpoints), so it is off until real consoles have shown it safe.

### New in 86: the CARD MANAGER
- **Square on a memory card** in Memory Files (or Triangle on a card image): every save with its size, **delete**, **back up the card to a VMC**, **write a VMC's saves to card 1 or 2**, **erase every game save** (boot loaders and system folders kept) and **format** (never the card RIPPS2 runs from). Destructive steps take two screens, the last one START only.
- Neutrino gets its automatic `-logo` first, NHDDL's order.

### New in 85: PS1 on real consoles, 704-wide modes, CD hints
- **A launch report**: just before POPSTARTER or Ember takes over, RIPPS2 writes `mc0:/RIPPS2/LAUNCH.TXT` (what it starts, its size and CRC, its arguments, the files beside it). If a PS1 game will not start on your console, open it in Memory Files and post a photo.
- POPSTARTER launches without Sony's `POPS.ELF` and `POPS_IOX.PAK` say so first, instead of a black screen.
- The 704-wide video modes draw in one pass (they could freeze the console). The CD player's hints stay on screen.

### New in 84: RiptOPL's latest
- 33 upstream commits: POPSTARTER's memory card folder only made when needed, PS1 messages that name the missing file, cheats on both cores, a VMC made on a game's first launch, Neutrino's argument preview, list labels you can turn off, MX4SIO ZSO fixes.

### Your sounds
**[The sound map](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2#the-sound-ripps2-was-made-with)** shows every event's sound. BIOS Sounds > Rip fills the menu sounds on the console; **[RIPPS2 Audio Studio](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/tree/main/tools/audio-studio)** does the rest on your PC (boot, launch, music).

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Alpha: keep your usual loader close by.

commit.message: Copy bounded unaligned upload rows with paired loads
Copy bounded unaligned upload rows with paired loads
Stream bounded upload rows with aligned quadword loads
Apply GP1 DMA control while the native worker is parked

Keep main focused on PSXCore and retain standalone tools on tester

Preserve the standalone tester, inventory probe, and their build support on the existing tester branch. Remove those applications from main and ignore local development copies.

Publish buffered interlaced display descriptor changes

Mark the native display descriptor dirty after the existing NTSC PS15/480 tuple guard. This lets the native caller publish the completed output bank through its existing GS completion path before subsequent uploads, while retaining masks, commands, waits and nonmatching-mode fallbacks.
Fix signed INTPL geometry interpolation in POPS
Increase adapter capacity and report startup planner failures
Precompute generated memory addresses by default

Add optional DMA, GP1 and empty GP0 flush optimizations

Preserve fewer wide temporaries in DMA accounting, reject ineligible GP1 commands before the full save, and reduce the empty GP0 flush path. Keep all three new options disabled by default and retain existing accounting, ownership checks, and fixed code bounds.

Enable DMA, GP1 and GP0 flush optimizations by default

Set root/runtime build defaults and assembly fallbacks to enabled. Preserve explicit disable overrides. Default-enabled and disabled builds match the previously verified enabled candidate and prior default loadable programs respectively.

Add optional smaller GP0 submission register saves

Reuse the overwritten return-value register for publisher calculations, removing one wide save/restore pair per submission. Preserve the original stack layout, command guards, native semaphore sequence and subsequent helper addresses. Keep NP_GP0_PUBLISH_TWO_TEMPS disabled by default pending gameplay validation.

Enable smaller GP0 submission saves by default

Enable NP_GP0_PUBLISH_TWO_TEMPS in root/runtime build defaults and its assembly fallback. Retain explicit disable support. The default and disabled builds match the previously verified candidate and baseline loadable programs.

Build 104: Arabic and Persian drawn right to left, letters joined

RIPPS2 draws text glyph by glyph from the left with no shaping engine, so
Arabic and Persian showed their letters unjoined and backwards. fntsys now
hands any string with right-to-left letters to ripps2Rtl (ripps2tr.c): each
Arabic letter becomes the presentation form its neighbours call for (lam with
alef as one ligature, ZWNJ stopping a join, vowel marks passed over), and
each line is laid out right to left, Latin words and numbers (with their %,
. and :) kept in reading order and brackets turned round. Text is measured
from the same joined letters and wrapped before it is turned, so wrapped
hints read top to bottom.

A mark with no advance that its font draws right of the pen (DejaVu's Arabic
vowel marks, Noto Sans Lao's vowels and tone marks: placed by OpenType, which
fntsys does not read) is now centred over the letter before it, a second mark
above stacking over the first.

The pack carries RIPPS2's own font for Arabic and Persian (DejaVu Sans 2.37
cut to Latin-1, the Arabic block and both presentation-form blocks: upstream's
cut had none of the joined forms) and Noto Sans Lao 2.003 for Laotian, each
with its licence text (elf/lang/fonts, make_lang_fonts.py). Upstream's older
Persian lines were stored pre-joined in an order made for another renderer;
the pack leaves those 248 out and Persian.yml has them written plain.

The joining table is generated from Unicode's data (make_arabic_forms.py).
The build 104 host test checks ripps2Rtl against vectors from a Python twin,
and Lao line breaks (never before a vowel or tone mark of the letter before,
nor after a vowel written ahead of its letter).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 104: Laotian

Lao: 779 of 800 strings and the 480 settings upstream's file lacks (it had 180
real lines), in the terms upstream uses, with spaces between phrases as Lao
writes them. Drawn with Noto Sans Lao (in the pack since the last commit), its
vowel and tone marks centred over their letters, and line breaks kept off the
marks and the vowels that belong to a letter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 104: RTL and Lao in the notes; the Lao pack drops RiptOPL's half-Thai lines

The changelog, README and plan say Arabic and Persian are drawn right to left
and joined, and Laotian is done. RiptOPL's Lao overlay has 9 lines half in
Thai, which Noto Sans Lao has no letters for: the pack leaves them out and
elf/lang/Laotian.yml translates them. The plan maps RIPDISC onto the code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 104: a full stop after a number stays with the right-to-left line

The lab's Persian take showed "MemCard PRO2." with its full stop on the
number's side: a . , : / + or - now joins a number only between two digits
(1.5, 12:00, 3/4), and % only beside one, as Unicode's bidi rules have it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 105: RIPDISC, a disc to storage or files from Launch Disc

After 4.2 s on Launch Disc a glass panel offers RIPDISC for a disc it can
rip; SELECT held 4.2 s opens a confirm step with the size and the place,
then START rips. PS2 games go to an ISO in a drive's CD or DVD folder (1 GB
parts and ul.cfg when over 4 GB on a drive that may be FAT32), PS1 games to
a BIN and CUE for Ember. Audio CDs and DVD videos go through Memory Files:
RIPPED on the clipboard, PASTE in the folder picked, an audio CD's folder
then named on the keyboard. AUDIO and MEDIA get a README.txt, and every
.ogg or .wav in AUDIO is music whatever its name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 105: a dual layer DVD's size found as OPL finds it

ps2sdk's EE libcdvd has no sceCdReadDvdDualInfo. Layer 1's own volume
descriptor sits at the sector layer 0's gives as its size, as OPL reads a
dual layer ISO: one quick read there, no retries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 105: a game with no title rips to <ID>.iso

With no title in the metadata and a disc label that is only its ID again
(POINIES POIN's is SCPS_150.13), the ISO was SCPS_150.13.SCPS_150.13.iso;
it is now SCPS_150.13.iso, whose ID OPL reads from inside. The plan gets
the user's power-off item for the in-game menu (build 106).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 105: the rip's time before START, learned per storage; RIPDISC in 33 languages

The confirm step says how long the rip will take: a careful guess for the
kind of storage and disc until a rip has measured this console, then what
that rip really ran at, kept in the settings (ripdisc_kbs_<storage>_<cd|dvd>).
The running estimate shows hours past 90 minutes. Lab: POINIES POIN ripped
from PCSX2's drive to a fresh exFAT HDD image is byte for byte the source
(md5 7e7a1db3...). RIPDISC's 38 new strings are translated in every language.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 106: POWER OFF in the in-game menu; the star on the left and keys for the list's row icons

The in-game menu's last choice turns the PS2 off, on a second press as
EXIT GAME leaves (a disc game keeps the ROM's power button and says so).
A starred game's star now sits left by default, in its own column, with
Settings > Game Sources > Starred Games Star (Theme, Left, Right, Hidden);
a theme's row icon moves to the row's end when the star is on the left.
New ItemsList keys: star, star_image, highlight (bar, line, none),
decorator_all and decorator_ps2 / _ps1 / _app. Translated in every language.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 107: SEARCH in Memory Files, where MC EXPLOIT INSTALLER was

The settings grid's fourth tile searches every drive the browser lists for
a file or folder name (any case), breadth first, one folder open at a time,
ten levels down, 150 results; back stops it. A result opens the tree where
it is, the cursor on it. New magnifier icon in the grid atlas. Also folds in
the build 105 fix CI found (rdMinutes declared before rdTick uses it).
Translated in every language; the installer's strings are gone from them.

The user's decisions of 10/19-10/20, every word on screen, rolls and slots,

Build 108: RIPSHOT, screenshots from the in-game menu; the menu silent and on by default; SCRn

SCREENSHOT is the in-game menu's third choice: the frame on screen when the
menu opened, read back from GS memory by ee_core, written over plain SIF DMA
(no RPC while the game is paused) to the game's roll in MEDIA/RIPSHOT on a
BDM drive (USB, exFAT HDD, MX4SIO, iLink), 6 slots a game, a blank roll kept
ready. ART, MEDIA or BOTH, with the names the files will have; SAVE fades the
menu off, KEEP / DELETE. Developing to 8-bit palette PNGs (median cut, ART at
250 x 188, MEDIA full size): Manual from the roll pages in Memory Files (VIEW,
ACTIONS), or Auto in the background. The menu is silent (SPU2 hushed, every
voice held) and RESUME puts the frame under the panel back.

The menu is on by default (a one-time switch for older configs) with its own
settings page (In-Game Menu, RIPSHOT, Develop Shots), each choice with its own
hint; disabled settings rows read dimmed. The SCRn theme key shows every shot
in turn (boxes one shot apart, slides the next shot each round): RIPPS2's info
page, RIPGRID and RIPFLOW use it. MEDIA's README explains RIPSHOT.

Also: the IOPRP image device is iprp (games hung in PCSX2 with its host
filesystem on), the menu switches GSM's data breakpoint off while open, a
picture taller than the TV raster stops at 480 / 576 lines, the menu's stack
and font sit after the modules. Translated in every language. CI uploads
ee_core.map with the symbols.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build 108: found while making the reel (the info page knows a game, new shots show at once, PNGs checked)

The reel takes found four things before release. A device rescan rebuilds the
game list under an open info page, and the info group, the slideshow, the shot
show and the art fades keyed on the row's address, so all the page's art faded
in again: they key on the game's id and title now. After Auto developed shots,
the art cache still held its earlier "absent" answers, so the info page showed
none: developing ART re-opens them. Once, an ART PNG reached the drive with an
empty directory entry and held its number: each developed PNG's size on the
drive is compared with what was written, with one more try, and an empty file
counts as a free number. SCRn finds the shots in order, _SCR first, whatever
order the reads come back in, and shows only a shot known to be there.

From testers (10/19-10/20). MMCE: a card's game list is kept on the card

+"""The Arabic joining-forms table in RiptOPL's src/ripps2tr.c (RIPPS2 build 104), made from Unicode's own data.
+
+Each Arabic letter that has presentation forms (U+FB50..U+FDFF, U+FE70..U+FEFF) gets its isolated, final, initial
+and medial forms; a letter with no initial or medial form joins to the letter before it only (alef, dal, reh, waw,
+...). Lam with alef is a ligature of its own, kept apart in ripps2tr.c. Run it and paste the output between the
+GENERATED markers:
+
+    python3 elf/lang/make_arabic_forms.py
+"""
+import unicodedata
+
+FORMS = ('isolated', 'final', 'initial', 'medial')
+
+
+def table():
+    found = {}
+    # forms B first: the standard letters' main forms; forms A then adds the Persian and Urdu letters
+    for c in list(range(0xFE70, 0xFF00)) + list(range(0xFB50, 0xFE00)):
+        d = unicodedata.decomposition(chr(c)).split()
+        if len(d) != 2 or d[0].strip('<>') not in FORMS:
+            continue
+        base = int(d[1], 16)
+        if not 0x0620 <= base <= 0x06FF:
+            continue
+        slot = found.setdefault(base, [0, 0, 0, 0])
+        k = FORMS.index(d[0].strip('<>'))
+        if slot[k] == 0:
+            slot[k] = c
+    return found
+
+
+def main():
+    rows = table()
+    print('// GENERATED by ps2-pillars elf/lang/make_arabic_forms.py (Unicode %s): base, isolated, final, initial, '
+          'medial' % unicodedata.unidata_version)
+    print('static const u16 trArab[][5] = {')
+    for base in sorted(rows):
+        iso, fin, ini, med = rows[base]
+        print('    {0x%04X, 0x%04X, 0x%04X, 0x%04X, 0x%04X}, // %s' % (base, iso, fin, ini, med, unicodedata.name(chr(base))))
+    print('};')
+    print('// GENERATED END')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+
+- DejaVuSans-Arabic.ttf: DejaVu Sans 2.37 cut to Latin-1, the Arabic block and both presentation-form blocks. RIPPS2
+  joins Arabic and Persian letters itself (ripps2Rtl in RiptOPL's src/ripps2tr.c) into those presentation forms, so
+  the font must carry all of them; upstream's font_Arabic is a cut without them.
+- NotoSansLao-Regular.ttf: Noto Sans Lao 2.003 (hinted), as released.
+
+Both come from their projects' own GitHub releases (downloaded once by hand; the user approved the sources on
+2026-10-19): github.com/dejavu-fonts/dejavu-fonts (dejavu-sans-ttf-2.37.zip) and github.com/notofonts/lao
+(NotoSansLao-v2.003.zip). Their licences go beside them and into the language pack.
+
+    python3 elf/lang/make_lang_fonts.py <dejavu-sans-ttf-2.37.zip> <NotoSansLao-v2.003.zip>
+"""
+import io
+import os
+import sys
+import zipfile
+
+from fontTools import subset
+from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+OUT = os.path.join(HERE, 'fonts')
+ARABIC = (list(range(0x20, 0x100)) + list(range(0x0600, 0x0700)) + list(range(0xFB50, 0xFE00)) +
+          list(range(0xFE70, 0xFF00)) + list(range(0x2010, 0x2028)) + [0x200C, 0x200D])
+
+
+def main(dejavu_zip, lao_zip):
+    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
+    z = zipfile.ZipFile(dejavu_zip)
+    font = TTFont(io.BytesIO(z.read('dejavu-sans-ttf-2.37/ttf/DejaVuSans.ttf')))
+    opts = subset.Options()
+    opts.layout_features = []  # RIPPS2 draws the presentation forms themselves, no GSUB/GPOS
+    opts.name_IDs = ['*']
+    opts.name_languages = ['*']
+    opts.notdef_outline = True
+    opts.hinting = False

+    sub.populate(unicodes=ARABIC)

+    font.save(os.path.join(OUT, 'DejaVuSans-Arabic.ttf'))
+    with open(os.path.join(OUT, 'LICENSE-DejaVu.txt'), 'wb') as f:
+        f.write(z.read('dejavu-sans-ttf-2.37/LICENSE'))
+
+    z = zipfile.ZipFile(lao_zip)
+    with open(os.path.join(OUT, 'NotoSansLao-Regular.ttf'), 'wb') as f:
+        f.write(z.read('NotoSansLao/hinted/ttf/NotoSansLao-Regular.ttf'))
+    with open(os.path.join(OUT, 'OFL-NotoSansLao.txt'), 'wb') as f:
+        f.write(z.read('OFL.txt'))
+    for name in sorted(os.listdir(OUT)):
+        print('%-28s %7d bytes' % (name, os.path.getsize(os.path.join(OUT, name))))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

+

+    if not ok:

+

+    """The function starting at sig, to its closing brace at the start of a line."""
+    i = src.index(sig)
+    j = src.index('\n}\n', i)
+    return src[i:j + 3]

+
+disc = rd('src/ripps2disc.c')
+ui = rd('src/ripps2ui.c')
+files = rd('src/ripps2files.c')
+sound = rd('src/sound.c')
+make = rd('Makefile')
+sb = rd('src/supportbase.c')

+check(re.search(r'FRONTEND_OBJS =[^\n]*\bripps2disc\.o\b', make) is not None, 'ripps2disc.o is in FRONTEND_OBJS')
+launch = ui[ui.index('void ripps2RenderLaunch(void)'):ui.index('void ripps2HandleInputLaunch(void)')]
+check('ripps2DiscRipRender();' in launch, 'LAUNCH DISC draws the RIPDISC panel')
+inp = ui[ui.index('void ripps2HandleInputLaunch(void)'):]
+check(inp.index('ripps2DiscRipInput()') < inp.index('getKeyOn(KEY_R1)'), 'the panel takes SELECT before the page does')
+worker = fn(ui, 'static void discPollWorker(void)')
