+check('RIPPS2_DISC_PS1' in worker and 'RIPPS2_DISC_ESR' in worker and 'RIPPS2_DISC_VIDEO' in worker, 'every disc kind is told')

+# Build 107 is RIPPS2 v1.0.7 beta: RIPDISC rips your discs, RIPPS2 in 33 languages, Power Off in the in-game menu, Search in Memory Files and the star on the left.
+
+## Get it
+- [Download the latest RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/latest/download/RIPPS2.elf) (this link always gets the newest build), [RIPPS2-languages.zip](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/latest/download/RIPPS2-languages.zip) for your language, and [the theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest/download/RIPPS2-themes.zip) (edition 107: replace your Adapt folders)
+- [The psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) and [the beta reel](https://youtu.be/LPjdK_E1jjM)
+
+## RIPDISC
+- **Launch Disc rips the disc in the drive.** After 4.2 s a glass panel offers RIPDISC; hold SELECT until its ring fills. The confirm step shows the size, **how long it should take** and where it goes; START rips.
+- **PS2 games** become an ISO in your DVD or CD folder (over 4 GB on a stick: OPL's 1 GB parts with ul.cfg). **PS1 games** a BIN and CUE for Ember. **Audio CDs and DVD videos** go through Memory Files: the clipboard says RIPPED, PASTE where you want them (a new MEDIA folder by default).
+- The time estimate learns your console's real speed from your first rip. Any WAV or OGG in AUDIO is now menu music by its own name.
+
+## Everything else
+- **33 languages**, Arabic and Persian right to left with joined letters, Lao in its own font: copy `LNG` from RIPPS2-languages.zip, then Settings > Display Settings > Language.
+- **Power Off** is the in-game menu's last choice (second press turns the PS2 off).
+- **SEARCH FILES** in Memory Files' settings grid (Start in the browser) finds any file or folder by name on every started drive.
+- **The star sits at the start of the row** now; Settings > Game Sources > Starred Games Star moves it right or hides it. Themes get new list keys (star, highlight, row icons).
+- RiptOPL brought up to 10/18/2026 underneath (548 upstream commits) and the version line tells the truth.
+
+## Test list
+- **Rip a PS2 DVD to a USB stick** (under 4 GB): was the estimate close? Does the game show and launch from Storage?
+- **Rip a PS2 game over 4 GB to a USB stick:** does it land as ul.* parts and launch?
+- **Rip to the internal exFAT HDD:** how long did it take, and did the next estimate match it?
+- **Dual-layer DVD** (a big late-era game): is the size right and does the ISO boot?
+- **Rip an audio CD:** MEDIA, PASTE, START. Do the WAVs play on a PC? Copy one into AUDIO: is it in Settings > Audio Settings > Music?
+- **Rip a PS1 game:** does Ember start the BIN and CUE from the PS1 list?
+- **Cancel a rip halfway:** is everything it wrote gone?
+- **Power Off in the in-game menu** (In-Game Menu on in Settings > General): does the second press turn the console off cleanly? The lab could not show this one.
+- **SEARCH FILES:** search a word from a save, a game and an ELF. Does Cross open the folder with the cursor on it?
+- **The star:** star a few games. Do the titles stay lined up? Try Right and Hidden too.
+- **Your language:** anything cut off, overlapping or untranslated? Arabic and Persian readers: does every line read right?
+- **720p and 1080i:** any of the above looking wrong in an HD mode?
+
+## Report
+Post in the [psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or here with your **console model**, your drives, and a **photo** of anything odd.

+# Build 109 is RIPPS2 v1.0.9 beta: an MMCE library lists at once, your settings can live on the internal HDD, and RIPSHOT (build 108) takes screenshots from the in-game menu. The lab has shown all it can; the test list is what only a real PS2 can tell us.
+
+## Get it
+- [Download the latest RIPPS2.elf](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/latest/download/RIPPS2.elf) (this link always gets the newest build), [RIPPS2-languages.zip](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2/releases/latest/download/RIPPS2-languages.zip) for your language, and [the theme pack](https://github.com/akilluminati47/RIPPS2-themes/releases/latest/download/RIPPS2-themes.zip) (edition 108: Adapt and Adapt Rx show every screenshot, replace your Adapt folders)
+- [The psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/)
+
+## MMCE boots fast (109)
+- **A big MMCE library lists at once.** The card keeps RIPPS2's last list of its games (`RIPPS2.LST`, beside CD and DVD): at boot the games show from it straight away, then the card is read again in the background and the list follows whatever changed. 180 games took about 5 minutes on every boot.
+- **The pads keep working while the card is read.** MMCE shares its bus with the controllers; the scan now pauses after every game so you can move around while it works.
+
+## Save Settings To (109)
+- **Settings > General > Save Settings To:** Memory Card (as before), **Internal HDD** (a RIPPS2 folder on the internal exFAT HDD, else the APA HDD's OPL partition, read first at boot) or Custom Path. Each choice has its own hint; with no internal HDD it says so and changes nothing.
+- **Settings pages:** a page's title stands clear of the line under it (it sat on the line and lost its descenders).
+
+## RIPSHOT (108)
+- **SCREENSHOT is the in-game menu's third choice** (L1+L2+R1+R2+SELECT+START): the exact frame that was up when the menu opened, no menu in it. **ART** (theme screenshot art), **MEDIA** (full-size PNG) or **BOTH**, then **SAVE**, **KEEP** or **DELETE**.
+- 6 shots a game wait on its roll in `MEDIA/RIPSHOT`. **Develop Shots: Manual** develops them from Memory Files, **Auto** in the background once you are back in RIPPS2. For now: games on USB, the exFAT HDD, MX4SIO and iLink.
+- **New theme key `SCRn`:** every shot a game has, in turn. The info page, RIPGRID, RIPFLOW, Adapt and Adapt Rx use it.
+
+## Everything else
+- **The in-game menu is on by default and silent**: the game's sound holds still while it is open, and RESUME gives back the exact frame. Settings > General > In-Game Menu is its own page; a row another setting switches off reads dimmed.
+- The info page no longer blinks when a rescan rebuilds the list, and a shot developed while RIPPS2 runs shows at once.
+- The new words in all 33 languages.
+
+## Test list
+- **MMCE, a big library (100+ games):** boot twice. On the second boot, do the games show at once? How long until the list stops changing?
+- **MMCE while it reads:** on a first boot (or after adding games), can you move, open the START menu and change pages while the list fills?
+- **MMCE changes:** add and remove a game on your PC, then boot. Does the list catch up by itself? Does a different card or a card switch show the right games?
+- **Boot to the game list:** from your loader to a list you can move in, with your usual drives. Faster than build 107? Tell us the seconds.
+- **Save Settings To > Internal HDD on the exFAT HDD:** change a setting, Save Changes, power off, take your memory cards out, boot. Are your settings still there?
+- **Internal HDD on an APA HDD:** same test. Does it say SETTINGS SAVED, and do they come back after a power cycle?
+- **Settings pages on your TV:** is every page title clear of its line, in 480i and in 480p/720p/1080i?
+- **RIPSHOT on a console:** a game on USB, the exFAT HDD, MX4SIO or iLink. Is the developed shot the frame you paused on? How long does the menu take to open?
+- **480p, 1080i and PAL games:** shots the right size, nothing torn or shifted?
+- **The silent menu:** open and close it in a game with music and speech. Any skip, loop, crackle or desync after RESUME?
+- **Menu music after RIPDISC or a game:** does the BGM come back every time? If it goes missing or glitches, tell us what you did just before.
+- **Power Off in the in-game menu:** does the second press turn the console off cleanly?
+
+## Report
+Post in the [psx-place thread](https://www.psx-place.com/threads/ripps2-a-ps2-front-end-in-one-elf-launch-disc-storage-memory-files.51316/) or here with your **console model**, your drives (MMCE model and firmware too), and a **photo** of anything odd.

+- **MMCE, USB, the exFAT HDD, MX4SIO, iLink and SMB** keep their last game list (`RIPPS2.LST`, beside CD and DVD): the games show the moment the drive answers, then the drive is read again the next time you are idle on Storage and the list follows whatever changed.

+

+- **Settings > General > Save Settings To:** Memory Card, Internal HDD, **USB Drive, MX4SIO, iLink, MMCE** or Custom Path, each with its own hint. A drive is saved by its type, so at boot only that drive's driver loads. A drive that is not connected says so and nothing changes.

+- **A USB stick plugged in with Internal HDD chosen:** do the settings still come from the HDD?
+- **Info page:** press Left / Right through your games. Does every one show its size?
+- **RIPSHOT on a console:** a game on USB, the exFAT HDD, MX4SIO or iLink. Is the developed shot the frame you paused on, in 480p, 1080i and PAL games too?
+- **The silent menu:** any skip, loop, crackle or desync after RESUME?
+- **Menu music after RIPDISC or a game:** does the BGM come back every time?

+

commit.message:
Release alpha.18

The console panel shows the rich presence line, and a setting keeps
unlock notices off the TV. LIVE splits achievements and leaderboards
into sub-tabs, with a badge grid and a ring for the unlock mode; GAME
gets the same grid. The hardcore flag from the Web API is fixed.
opl moves to c6e14e6b: no cheat engine, and watch list chunks arrive
intact.

commit.message: Fix the in-game SMAP TX descriptor buffer address

Remove the cheat engine and fix watch list chunk parsing

OPL-RA no longer carries PS2RD, reads no CHT files and has no cheat
menu. A list chunk whose data started with a whitespace byte lost that
byte, and the console refused the whole list.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the RA snapshot going when Mode 6 turns the IGR off

RA_OnVblank ran only from the IGR's VBLANK_END handler, and Mode 6
skips Install_IGR, so a game set to Mode 6 sent no telemetry at all.
Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus needs that mode: it takes the
IGR's padOpen patch for tampering and hides collectibles (xerabora
issue #15).

Under Mode 6 syshook now installs a handler that calls RA_OnVblank and
nothing else: no IGR thread, no padOpen patch, no CreateThread/ExecPS2
hooks. A reset asked for over the network has nothing to carry it out
in that mode, so IGR_RequestReset drops it.

Built, not run on hardware.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

PS1: achievements under POPStarter

A PS1 image in POPS/<name>.VCD on a block device is listed with the PS2
games, marked PS1, hashed the way rcheevos hashes a PS1 disc and
launched through POPStarter (krHACKen r13) as mass:/POPS/XX.<name>.ELF.
Nothing of OPL runs under POPS, so the watch list travels inside
POPS/MODULE_9.IRX: OPL writes a copy of rapops with the IP
configuration, the serial and the list in its config block, POPStarter
loads it on the IOP after its own reset. rapops brings up DEV9, SMAP,
the TCP/IP stack and raudp as under a PS2 game, then starts rapull,
which reads the PS1 RAM windows through sceSifGetOtherData at 60 Hz and
hands the snapshots to raudp. The first request waits 25 seconds: one
during POPS's boot leaves the screen black.

POPStarter reads the game's device with its own driver. OPL puts the
BDMAssault pair for the device on the memory card before the launch
(mc?:/POPSTARTER/, RA_BDMA.TXT names the variant): mx4sio, ata, ilink.
USB stays on the built-in FAT32 driver unless "PS1 USB drive is exFAT"
is on in Settings; OPL cannot tell the formats apart, and the usbexfat
pair stalls POPS on its first video from a FAT32 stick.

Confirmed on hardware: Blade from a FAT32 stick and from an exFAT
drive, 60 snapshots a second, achievements unlock. Not done: PS1 from
MMCE, an APA HDD or a share; a second device of the same kind. The
MX4SIO, iLink and exFAT HDD pairs follow RiptOPL and have not been
run here.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

RA: name the sector source instead of a sentinel fd and a flag

read_at() took a file descriptor, with -100 standing for the drive and
a global flag switching it to VCD sectors around each call. It now
takes a struct ra_src with the descriptor and its kind. The PS1 code
reads SYSTEM.CNF in one place for the list and for the hash.

Host test: Blade.VCD 3e64b72f... (RA 14491) and Dynasty Warriors 2
29e392c7... (RA 19047), both unchanged. cppcheck finds nothing in the
changed lines.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

PS1: drop the PS1/PS2 order setting

The build with it hung in the menu on hardware, and two probes showed
the hang is not in the POPS/ scan. Removed: the setting, the group and
sort-key fields on menu items, the sort by them. The sort is stock again.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

PS1: list POPS/*.VCD with the PS2 games and launch POPStarter

The BDM pages append every POPS/<name>.VCD at the device root, marked
"PS1", with the serial read out of the image's SYSTEM.CNF. Launching
one copies POPS/POPSTARTER.ELF to XX.<name>.ELF if it is missing and
loads it as mass:/POPS/XX.<name>.ELF: POPStarter parses its argv[0],
and the SDK loader sets argv[0] to the path it loads. First USB device
only for now. The RA check hashes the VCD and asks the PC as for PS2.

A new UI setting, "PS1 and PS2 order": mixed by name, PS2 first or
PS1 first. The sort now compares game names, not badged text.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

RA: hash PS1 images for POPS (.VCD)

raHashVcd reads a VCD the way rc_hash_psx reads a PS1 disc: skip the
1 MiB POPS header, map 2048-byte offsets onto 2352-byte MODE2 sectors,
take BOOT from SYSTEM.CNF (PSX.EXE if there is none), size from the
PS-X EXE header plus 2048, MD5 of name and bytes. Directory names now
compare case-insensitively, as rcheevos does for both consoles.

Not called yet. Host test on Blade (USA): 3e64b72f..., RA game 14491.

commit.message:
VMC: opt-in Rebuild for a card too fragmented for the native core (#986)

An existing card that holds saves but is in too many pieces for native
mcemu (BDM: more than one extent; HDD: PFS map too long) was skipped at
every launch with no way to fix it from the loader. The per-game VMC
dialog now offers Rebuild for exactly that case, after confirmation:

- genvmc gets a copy mode (VMC_CREATE_REBUILD): it creates <name>.new
  exclusively with the same reservation a new card gets (BDM one extent
  via VMC_ALLOC, HDD one PIOCALLOC, refusal = no room), copies every
  byte, reads both back and compares, and on BDM confirms the extent.
  It only accepts a .new target and derives the .bin source itself, so
  it can never write or remove a card; the card is opened read-only.
- The EE (src/vmcrebuild.c) proves .bak/.new absent by reading the
  folder (PFS rename replaces its target), runs the launch's own layout
  check on the copy, then renames card -> .bak and copy -> .bin, undoing
  the first rename if the second fails and syncing PFS after renames.
  Only the copy this rebuild made is ever removed, and only while the
  card is confirmed in place. Card and backup are never deleted.

Host tests: test_vmc_rebuild.py drives the real genvmc and EE code over
an in-memory fs with a fault at every step on BDM and PFS (mutation-
checked); test_vmc_rebuild_fatfs.py fragments a real card on FAT32 and
exFAT images, gets "no room" with nothing changed, then rebuilds it to
one extent with identical bytes and the backup kept across remount.
ZERO hardware testing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add compat Mode 8 Slow Reads: Accurate Reads at the CD rate for DVD (#924)

Tales of the Abyss loses its music and SFX after Shurrey Hill and corrupts
SFX boarding the flying ship. Testers on the psx-place OPL thread found it
plays clean at <=1000KB/s and breaks at >=1200KB/s; OPL 0.9's Mode 1
(~900KB/s) fixed it. Our Mode 1 throttles DVD media to 33512 ticks/sector
(~2200KB/s), so it stays too fast.

Honouring the game's requested spindle speed was ruled out: nothing in our
code shows what this title asks for, and changing how sceCdRead's mode is
read would change the read rate of every Mode 1 game that passes a
non-maximum speed.

Mode 8 (OPL core only, greyed under Neutrino) turns Accurate Reads on and
reads DVD media at the CD rate (81920 ticks/sector, ~900KB/s). Mode 1 alone
keeps CD 81920 / DVD 33512, so no other game changes speed. No title
default is added until the reporter confirms on hardware.

COMPAT_MODE_COUNT goes 6 -> 8 so the per-game screen reads and saves bit 7.
That also makes the existing Mode 7 checkbox (Neutrino -gc=7) save: it has
been drawn since rebuild-08 but its bit was dropped on save.

Host test test_accurate_read_rate.py compiles the real rate function and
pins the ticks/sector for CD/DVD with and without Mode 8.

commit.message:
fix(ilink): log back in after an IOP reset; offer only a ready drive (#1018)

i.LINK games listed on every core, Ember booted, and native OPL (PS2
logo, then nothing), Neutrino and POPSTARTER did not. Ember is the only
core that never resets the IOP.

ps2sdk's IEEE1394_bd never logs out (SBP2_LOGOUT_REQUEST is defined but
never sent) and an IOP reset ends it without warning, so the next driver
finds the drive still holding the old exclusive login for its SBP-2
reconnect hold: 2^0 = 1 s for the RECONNECT(0) every login here asks
for, longer on bridges that round it up. It tried 5 LOGINs 200 ms apart
(~0.8 s), inside that hold, and only the next bus reset retries, which a
running game never causes: the device never attached and CDVDMAN waited
forever.

- initConfigureSBP2Device: keep asking every 200 ms for up to 5 s of
  elapsed time (a time budget, so slow refusals cannot stretch it).
- scsi_warmup: TEST UNIT READY at most 300 times, 100 ms apart (30 s for
  a cold 3.5" drive); a block length of 0 is a failure.
- scsi_connect: publish the device only after a successful warm-up; a
  failed attempt frees its slot for the next bus reset.

Vendored as modules/ilink/IEEE1394_bd (ORIGIN.txt: pin, local changes);
the Makefile embeds this build, full or mini, instead of the SDK's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

VMC rebuild: say so when PFS cannot commit the swap instead of reporting success

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(ilink): simulate the post-reset login hold and unready drives

test_ilink_bd_reset.py compiles initConfigureSBP2Device (extracted) and
all of scsi.c (mini variant) against simulated drives and a simulated
clock: logins refused for 1, 1.6 and 4.5 s, a drive that never lets go,
slow refusals, TEST UNIT READY never ready or ready after 50 polls,
failed INQUIRY / READ CAPACITY, block length 0, and slot reuse after
failures. The SDK sources fail 12 of the checks; wired into flavours.yml.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

build(neutrino): ship RiptOPL's i.LINK driver in the Neutrino bundle (#1018)

Neutrino's in-game environment loads its own iLinkman + IEEE1394_bd_mini
after its IOP reboot (config/bsd-ilink.toml), the same SDK code with the
same post-reset login race. The required ps2dev-latest build stages
modules/ilink/IEEE1394_bd/IEEE1394_bd_mini.irx as its own artifact (not
rolling/, which is published wholesale); publish-rolling replaces
neutrino/modules/IEEE1394_bd_mini.irx with it and refuses to package if
upstream stops shipping that file or the copy does not land.
package_release_app.py requires the file in ordinary packages; the RA kit
keeps ORBIT's Neutrino unmodified. docs/NEUTRINO.md says what changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(theme): make PSBBN Flow match the PSBBN-DP Game Collection

The built-in <PSBBN Flow> only borrowed the Collection fan: a plain blue wash, a
large portrait cover, flat covers spread across the screen, the title and count
in the bottom-left, and no selection highlight. It now follows the PSBBN
Definitive Project's Game Collection, measured from CosmicScale's published
videos (no PSBBN code or artwork):

- black header and button-hint bands with thin rules, a blue nebula stage
  (new 8-bit 160x120 psbbn_bg texture, filtered up) and a still star field
- the page list where PSBBN lists Collection and Disc, with the stacked
  Collection panel outline behind it
- a rounded square focal cover (art cropped to its centre square) with PSBBN's
  soft white rim; title above it, n/N count under its lower right corner
- a tail of covers turned away into the distance, drawn in perspective strips
  with perspective-correct art, darker and fading toward the far end
- the outgoing cover swells toward the viewer and fades; title and count hide
  while covers move and return when they settle

Drawing uses rmDrawTriangles plus a blended variant; 24-bit art fades through
the GS fixed blend factor because it has no alpha of its own. Per frame this
is under 200 triangles. The 25-frame cubic glide from #733/#977 is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(pops-ilink): log back in after POPSTARTER's IOP reset (#1018)

POPSTARTER resets the IOP and loads its i.LINK driver, usbhdfsd.irx.ilink
(modules/bdmassault/ilink_bd_assault: an older ps2sdk IEEE1394_bd plus
iLinkman), from the memory card. That driver never logs out of the drive
(SBP2_LOGOUT_REQUEST is defined but never sent), so after the reset the
drive still holds the previous driver's exclusive login for its SBP-2
reconnect hold: 1 s for the RECONNECT(0) every login asks for, longer on
bridges that round it up. It tried 5 LOGINs 200 ms apart (~0.8 s),
inside that hold, and only the next bus reset retries, which POPSTARTER
never causes.

Same three changes as OPL's own copy of the driver (PR #1022), with the
same constants and "RiptOPL" markers:

- initConfigureSBP2Device: keep asking every 200 ms for up to 5 s of
  elapsed time (GetSystemTime/SysClock2USec, already imported).
- scsi_warmup: TEST UNIT READY at most 300 times, 100 ms apart; a block
  length of 0 is a failure (the capacity printf divided by it). This
  older driver has no READ CAPACITY(16) path to guard.
- scsi_connect: offer the drive to BDM only after a successful warm-up;
  a failed attempt frees its slot for the next bus reset.

The cdvdman removal and everything else in the driver are unchanged.
test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py compiles the real scsi.c and the login
function against simulated drives and a simulated clock; on the
previous sources it fails 11 checks and crashes on block length 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

build(pops-ilink): ship the rebuilt usbhdfsd.irx.ilink; CI proves it (#1018)

Rebuilt modules/bdmassault/ilink_bd_assault with its own Makefile in the
PS2DEVPINNED container (ghcr.io/ps2dev/ps2dev@sha256:8fba50ec...): 21977
bytes, sha256 8f9a9e4e6984a58435fe7e24e1e5832f027dc537b3274bc4220245bbe1844714.
The same container rebuilds the previous 21609-byte binary (9b47d90b...)

Not tested on hardware.

commit.message:
fix(bdma): name an older release's device POPS/ pair instead of a card write error

A launch equip copied whatever usbd.irx.<mode> + usbhdfsd.irx.<mode> pair it
found first, then checked the card pair's sizes against vcdBdmaPairSig. A
device POPS/ folder still holding an older release's pair (the 21609-byte
usbhdfsd.irx.ilink after #1024) was copied on every launch, failed that
check, and toasted "Error writing the BDMA modules to the memory card".

The launch equips (vcdEnsureBdmaForLaunch, the USB fat32/exFAT dialog and
APA __common) now measure each candidate pair before copying -- by reading
it through on MMCE, which has no SEEK_END -- pass over a pair that is not
this release's, and keep searching the same seek order (custom dir, boot
POPS/, game device, other UDPFS sources, __common). With only an older pair
found they copy nothing, leave the card as it is, and show the new
BDMA_ERR_OLD toast. The launch still goes ahead. The Settings page's manual
equip is unchanged: it installs the pair the user chose.

Host test test_bdma_stale_pair.py compiles the real equip and launch code;
against the old source every stale case shows BDMA_ERR_IO after 4 card
copies. Not hardware-tested.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(udpfs): deliver the last byte of odd-sized reads (#1010)

smap_fifo_read() copied the PIO tail of a received frame as whole words
and then one u16, with no step for a single last byte. Every odd-length
reply -- the final packet of every odd-sized file read over UDPFS --
came back at the right size with its last byte left as whatever the
buffer held before.

The #1010 tester's Neutrino folder on mc1 shows exactly that: all 29
damaged files have an odd size and differ only in their last byte, and
no even-sized file is touched. The NUL that ended i_dev9_hidden.toml
stops Neutrino with "bad control char in comment" (his udptty log; the
same files fail the same way in Neutrino's own tomlc17 on a PC), so the
UDPFS driver never loads and every game resets to the browser. In
RiptOPL's own menu the lost byte breaks the IEND CRC of odd-sized PNG
covers read over UDPFS.

Read the tail as one whole word (the FIFO pads each frame to 4 bytes)
and store only its valid bytes. Upstream Neutrino master has the same
tail. test_udpfs_smap_fifo_tail.py compiles the real function against a
simulated FIFO and fails on the old code for every odd byte count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(lang): lock the language registry; show English for unsafe translations

Address the CodeRabbit review of #1017.

1. The registry is now a growable array whose entries can be replaced,
   and the IO worker changed it with no lock while the GUI thread read
   it. lngReadEntry grows, fills and replaces a path only under the GUI
   lock (old path freed after), nLanguages is published under it, and
   lngSetGuiValue copies the path under it and reads the file with the
   lock released. Every other reader runs on the IO worker or inside a
   locked GUI frame. The discovery and switch tests now fail on an
   unlocked realloc or a nested lock.

2. The audit checked printf tokens on the fork overlay only, though the
   upstream string wins. Run against upstream today, ten upstream
   strings differ from English, and several would crash: French
   AUTO_START_IN_N_SECS has %s for an int (the Auto Start countdown),
   and three Persian strings swap or add a %s. lngLoadFromFile now
   checks every loaded string (lngFormatFits) and uses the English one
   when its conversions would read other argument types; the same ones
   or fewer in order are kept. The audit checks the merged strings: an
   overlay mismatch fails --strict, an upstream one is a warning, so an
   upstream change cannot break the language build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+"""Accurate Reads (Mode 1) keeps its rates, and Slow Reads (Mode 8) gives a DVD title the CD rate (#924).
+
+Tales of the Abyss loses its music and SFX when the in-game reader runs at >=1200KB/s and plays clean at
+<=1000KB/s. Mode 1 throttles DVD media to 33512 IOP ticks per sector (~2200KB/s), so the title needs a
+slower rate, but every other Mode 1 game must keep the speed it has today.
+
+Compiles the real cdvdman_accu_read_ticks() from modules/iopcore/cdvdman/cdvdman.c against fake settings
+and pins the ticks per sector for CD and DVD media, with and without Slow Reads. Then checks the read loop
+uses it, sbPrepare maps Mode 8 onto the in-game flags, and the per-game screen saves and shows Mode 8.
+"""
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile

+"""A translated string must not read arguments its English string is not given.
+
+RiptOPL hands each translation to printf with the English string's arguments. Several upstream
+translations do not match them: French AUTO_START_IN_N_SECS has %s where English has %i (the
+Auto Start countdown then reads its int as a string pointer and crashes), Persian strings swap or
+add conversions. lngLoadFromFile now checks every loaded string with lngFormatFits and shows the
+English string instead of one that would misread its arguments.
+
+This compiles the real lngFormatArgs/lngFormatFits from src/lang.c and checks them against the
+upstream cases and the printf forms RiptOPL's strings use, and that lngLoadFromFile applies them.
+"""
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+source = (root / "src/lang.c").read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n")
+failures = []
+
+start = source.find("static int lngFormatArgs(")
+end = source.find("static int lngLoadFromFile(", start)
+if start < 0 or end < 0:
+    print("src/lang.c: lngFormatArgs/lngFormatFits not found before lngLoadFromFile")
+    sys.exit(1)
+guard = source[start:end]
+
+load = source[end:source.find("\n}\n", end) + 3]
+if not re.search(r"lngFormatFits\(newL\[i\], internalEnglish\[i\]\)", load):
+    failures.append("lngLoadFromFile does not check each loaded string with lngFormatFits")
+
+# (translation, English, fits)
+CASES = [
+    ("Lancement automatique dans %s...", "Auto start in %i s...", 0),  # upstream French: crash
+    ("Auto %i s", "Auto start in %i s...", 1),
+    ("% s ... % d", "%s ... %d", 1),  # upstream Cebuano: a space flag reads the same argument
+    ("no conversions", "%s %d", 1),  # upstream Japanese: fewer arguments are never misread
+    ("%s %d %d", "%s %d", 0),  # upstream TChinese: an argument that is not passed
+    ("%d %s", "%s %d", 0),  # upstream Persian: swapped
+    ("%s %s", "%s", 0),  # upstream Persian GAME_SETTINGS_REMOVED
+    ("100%% done %s", "%s", 1),
+    ("%1$s", "%s", 0),  # positional arguments are not understood: English is safer
+    ("%-10s|%5.2f", "%s|%f", 1),
+    ("%lu", "%u", 0),
+    ("%lu", "%lu", 1),
+    ("%lld", "%d", 0),
+    ("%hhd %hu %c %x", "%d %d %d %d", 1),
+    ("%d", "%*d", 1),
+    ("%*d", "%d", 0),
+    ("%p", "%s", 0),
+    ("%n", "%d", 0),
+    ("trailing %", "%d", 0),
+    ("%s", "not a format %", 1),  # English this check does not understand: left alone
+    ("", "", 1),
+]
+
+harness = r"""
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <string.h>
+""" + guard + r"""
+struct test_case { const char *translated, *english; int fits; };
+static const struct test_case cases[] = {
+@CASES@
+};
+int main(void)
+{
+    int failures = 0;
+    for (unsigned int i = 0; i < sizeof(cases) / sizeof(cases[0]); i++) {
+        int fits = lngFormatFits(cases[i].translated, cases[i].english);
+        if (fits != cases[i].fits) {
+            printf("\"%s\" for English \"%s\": %s, want %s\n", cases[i].translated, cases[i].english,
+                   fits ? "kept" : "replaced", cases[i].fits ? "kept" : "replaced");
+            failures++;
+        }
+    }
+    return failures != 0;
+}
+"""
+
+
+def c_string(text):
+    return '"' + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
+
+
+rows = ",\n".join("    {%s, %s, %d}" % (c_string(t), c_string(e), f) for t, e, f in CASES)
+with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+    tmp = Path(tmp)
+    program = tmp / "guard.c"
+    exe = tmp / ("guard.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "guard")
+    program.write_text(harness.replace("@CASES@", rows), encoding="utf-8")
+    build = subprocess.run(["cc", "-std=gnu99", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror", "-Wno-format-security",
+                            str(program), "-o", str(exe)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+    if build.returncode != 0:
+        failures.append("did not compile:\n" + build.stderr)
+    else:
+        run = subprocess.run([str(exe)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=20)
+        if run.returncode != 0:
+            failures += run.stdout.strip().splitlines() or ["exited %d" % run.returncode]
+
+if failures:
+    print("\n".join(failures))
+    sys.exit(1)
+print("Language format guard: translations that misread their arguments fall back to English")

+
+The release builds **33 external languages**, all now supplied with fork-specific

+Some newly introduced fork labels may still show English fallback: a complete

+including the most recently appended 60 UI labels; pass `--json` for a
+machine-readable report. The tool uses the same translation precedence as
+`make languages`, and reads `lng_src/` if `make download_lng` has been
+run. Run `python3 tools/audit_translations.py --strict` to reject invalid
+format placeholders and obsolete overlay keys without blocking valid
+English fallback. CI runs the strict audit on translation and source changes.
+It checks the strings that ship, upstream ones included. A fork overlay string
+with the wrong placeholders fails `--strict`. An upstream one is listed as a
+warning: RiptOPL checks every string in a `.lng` file when it loads it and
+shows the English string instead of any whose placeholders would read other
+arguments (for example upstream French "Auto start" has `%s` where English has
+`%i`, which crashed the countdown). Placeholders the same as English, or fewer
+of them in the same order, are kept.
+
+To translate recent strings, review the report, add genuinely localized text
+to each `lng_fork/<Language>.yml`, and rerun the audit. **Do not mark
+untranslated English copies as completed translations**. Preserve all
+`%s`, `%d`, `%i` placeholders and keep their order. Inspect the result
+on a PS2; a syntactically valid translation can still be confusing, truncated,
+or missing font glyphs. Missing status is distinct from broken packaging.

+## Translation provenance and review
+
+RIPPS2's keyed `labels:` maps contributed additional localized text for 32
+overlapping language names; Ryukyuan retains the existing RiptOPL overlay,
+because RIPPS2 has no Ryukyuan source. The imported overlay files credit
+Akilluminati47 and preserve RiptOPL's existing keys. The language compiler
+always prioritizes an already translated upstream community entry over the
+fork overlay. Compare source phrasing against the **current** `_base.yml`
+English definition before changing a translation: even correctly parsed
+strings can have stale feature descriptions. Review particularly UTF-8 glyphs,
+right-to-left rendering, and placeholders in each language on PS2 hardware.

+## Installing and selecting language files
+
+From the release matching your ELF, download `RIPTOPL-LANGS-*.zip` and
+extract your chosen `lang_<Language>.lng`. Copy its matching
+`font_<Language>.ttf` or `font_<Language>.otf` (if included) beside the
+language file. Keep the original filenames.
+
+Languages are discovered in this precedence order:
+
+1. **Beside RiptOPL's launched ELF (CWD)**, e.g.
+   `mass0:/APPS/APP_RIPTOPL/lang_French.lng`.
+2. **CWD/LNG/**, e.g. `mass0:/APPS/APP_RIPTOPL/LNG/lang_French.lng`.
+3. **Existing locations**, including `mc0:/OPL/` and each enabled
+   device's `LNG/` directory.
+
+The language menu shows a language only once: the higher-priority location
+wins when duplicates exist. Scans retry an initially inaccessible boot path
+after the storage drivers mount. Language registration grows dynamically rather
+than stopping at 15 files. Restart RiptOPL after copying files into folders
+already scanned during the current session.

+where available), confirm, and **Save Settings**. English is always built
+in; missing newer translations fall back to English. Games and OSDSYS keep

+## Rebuilding a card the native core cannot map
+
+A card that already holds saves but is too fragmented for the native core (on BDM: more than one extent; on the HDD: a PFS map longer than native mcemu holds) is skipped at launch. The per-game VMC dialog shows such a card as **Too fragmented for the native core** and offers a **Rebuild** button. It appears only for a valid 8/16/32/64 MB card on a BDM (FAT32/exFAT) or HDD source whose game uses the native core, and only when the layout check gives a definite answer; Neutrino maps cards its own way, and other stores cannot say how a card lies.
+
+Rebuild asks for confirmation, then:
+
+1. Refuses to start if `VMC/<name>.bak` or `VMC/<name>.new` already exists (absence is proven by reading the folder). Either may hold saves, so neither is ever overwritten; move it away on a PC and try again.
+2. genvmc creates `VMC/<name>.new` exclusively, with the same reservation a new card gets: on BDM the whole card as one extent through the versioned driver API (no room means the job stops at once); on the HDD every zone in one PIOCALLOC request, and here a refusal also stops the job.
+3. genvmc copies every byte of the card into the copy, then reads both back and compares them byte for byte. On BDM the driver then confirms one extent within the 32-bit sector range.
+4. The loader runs the launch's own layout check on the copy (BDM: one extent covering the card; HDD: the PFS map fits).
+5. Only then two renames swap them: the card becomes `VMC/<name>.bak`, the copy becomes `VMC/<name>.bin`. On the HDD the PFS cache is committed after the renames.
+
+The card itself is only ever opened read-only. On any failure or cancellation before the swap, only the `.new` file this rebuild created is removed, and the card is left as it was. Not enough unbroken free space is reported as such, with nothing changed. If the second rename fails, the first is undone. If a rename cannot be undone, both `.bak` (the old card) and `.new` (the verified copy) are kept and the dialog says so; rename one of them back to `.bin` on a PC. On the HDD, if PFS cannot commit the swap, the dialog says the change was not confirmed instead of reporting success. A copy is removed only while the card is confirmed under its own name. The loader never deletes the card or the backup: delete `VMC/<name>.bak` on a PC once the rebuilt card's saves check out. If power is lost between the two renames, `VMC/<name>.bak` holds the card.
+
+Host tests run genvmc's real request, worker, copy and verify code and the loader's real start, layout check and swap over an in-memory filesystem with a fault at every step: reservation refusal, card read error, short copy write, copy reading back different, failed close, driver layout failure, a copy whose layout fails or cannot be checked, each rename failing or reporting failure after it happened, a `.bak` or `.new` already present or appearing during the job, an unreadable folder, and an abort during the copy and during the verify, on both BDM and PFS. A second test writes a card interleaved with other files on disposable FAT32 and exFAT images (pinned FatFs, the shipped fragment walker and allocation patch), confirms the launch check calls it fragmented, gets "not enough unbroken free space" with nothing changed while no 8 MiB run is free, then rebuilds it to one extent with identical bytes and the old card kept as `.bak` across a remount. +#ifndef VMCREBUILD_H
+#define VMCREBUILD_H
+
+/* Rebuild a native VMC the native core cannot map (#986): a verified, reserved copy replaces the card,
+ * and the card is kept beside it as "<name>.bak". One rebuild at a time, like genvmc itself.
+ * Outcomes of vmcRebuildStart (0 = genvmc accepted the copy job) and vmcRebuildFinish. */
+enum vmc_rebuild_result {
+    VMC_REBUILD_DONE = 0,      // the card is the rebuilt copy; the old card is "<name>.bak"
+    VMC_REBUILD_FAILED = -1,   // nothing changed (the copy, if any was made, is gone)
+    VMC_REBUILD_NO_ROOM = -2,  // not enough unbroken free space for a mappable copy; nothing changed
+    VMC_REBUILD_ABORTED = -3,  // cancelled; nothing changed
+    VMC_REBUILD_LEFTOVER = -4, // "<name>.bak" or "<name>.new" is already there; never overwritten
+    VMC_REBUILD_STUCK = -5,    // a rename failed half way: "<name>.bak" and "<name>.new" are both kept
+    VMC_REBUILD_UNSYNCED = -6, // swapped, but PFS could not commit it: the old card is still "<name>.bak"
+};
+
+// The card at path (<prefix>VMC/<name>.bin, sizeMb MB) for the native core: 1 it maps, 0 it does not
+// but a rebuilt copy could (BDM fragmented, HDD PFS map too long), -1 the store cannot tell.
+int vmcRebuildLayout(const char *path, int sizeMb);
+// Start the copy job for the card at path. 0 = started; otherwise a vmc_rebuild_result.
+int vmcRebuildStart(const char *path, int sizeMb);
+// Once genvmc reports the started job finished: check the copy's layout and swap it in.
+int vmcRebuildFinish(int jobError);
+
+#endif

commit.message: App icon
Version 0.18.0
Classic View

Theme wallpapers: a global one and one per system

A background block can set `wallpaper` (PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 16 MB)
and `fit` (cover or stretch), drawn over the corners by the background
layer. The theme's shows on the systems grid and the virtual systems, a
system's own while its games are shown, cross-fading with the look.

Wallpapers are decoded by Godot on the thread pool, scaled to fit
2560x1080 (the 3D the background goes through is at most 1080 high), and
at most three are kept. A system's is fetched ahead once its card has
been focused for 0.15 s. The item shader reads them only while a grid
fades, so items still fade exactly into what's behind them.

On the export, PS2's 60 s scroll with its wallpaper on screen: GPU
0.18 -> 0.21 ms, frames, hitches and allocation unchanged, start-up
within the spread, textures +16 MB for two wallpapers
(docs/perf/wallpapers.md).

Generated with Claude Code under company AI usage policy

Theme the text over the grids from [ui.menu]

The heading's glow and subtitle, the hints, the centre message's glow and
the list layout's titles and highlight now follow the theme's menu colours
(OverlayPalette), instead of the launcher's blue on every theme. The
heading's title stays white. A theme setting no menu colour keeps the old
values exactly. No per-frame cost: scroll bench unchanged before and after.

Generated with Claude Code under company AI usage policy
fix emulator options
zoom fix
game template defaults
more clamshells
PS2 game template
Version 0.17.1

End what the update helper's publish leaves running

The 0.17.0 release's export waited 15 minutes after it had finished: MSVC's
linker, run by the helper's Native AOT publish, leaves vctip.exe (its
telemetry uploader) running, and it held Godot's output pipe, which the
console wrapper waits on. Local exports hung the same way.

Platform/ToolProcess runs the publish in a job object of its own and ends
whatever it left running as it exits; the export addon uses it.

Generated with Claude Code under company AI usage policy

Rescan the library without its media folders

Settings, Library has two rescans. "Rescan the library" (F5, and the scans
at launch) lists every ROM folder, and a system's media folder only when it
finds a game the library didn't have, so an unchanged library lists no media
folder; "Rescan the library and media" (Shift+F5) is the old full scan, for
files put in the media folder by hand. LibraryService.RescanAsync takes a
RescanMedia; a media folder change and saved ROM folders still index every
media folder they affect.

odyssey-scrape scan --quick and the nav-script step quick-rescan run it.
core-bench: an unchanged rescan with media 110.5 ms, the quick one 61.5 ms.

Generated with Claude Code under company AI usage policy
Version 0.17.0

Check for updates in the settings

Settings, Odyssey Launcher, Check for updates asks GitHub for the newest
release; a newer one is offered in a question, and yes downloads it beside
the launcher, checks its SHA-256 and unpacks it, then quits. OdysseyUpdater.exe,
a Native AOT helper shipped beside the launcher (published by the export
addon), waits for the launcher to quit, renames the new files into place
(putting the old version back if any rename fails), keeps the user's files,
and starts the launcher again with the same command line.

--update-feed and --open=update test it from a local folder.

Generated with Claude Code under company AI usage policy
PSP model
Scanning and logging tweaks

inspect-theme counts only the launcher's systems as a theme's cards

A logo set made for ES-DE carries logos for systems the launcher doesn't have, and alternates: Odyssey Vita's new
icons are 269 files, 210 of them valid ids, for 170 of the launcher's systems and collections.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bally Astrocade's id is astrocade, not astrocde

astrocde stays as a ROM folder alias and as MAME's machine name in the
emulator arguments. The emulators are renamed to match, Slab's logo now
matches by id, and a user-data migration moves existing favourites,
stats, matches, overrides and scrape requests to the new id.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Themes follow their repository's default branch, as in ES-DE

themes.json has no commit any more: a theme is reviewed once, when it's listed, and its author's pushes then reach
users as updates. A on an installed theme fetches and updates it, says when there's nothing new, and asks before
overwriting changes of the user's own; a broken push is refused and the clone reset. covers stays, optional.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

A theme's covers count a logo a system names once

Slab's and Odyssey Vita's logos/astrocade.webp is Bally Astrocade's ([systems.astrocde] logo), and was counted as a
system "astrocade" too, so inspect-theme said 172 system cards for 171.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

An in-app theme downloader, as ES-DE's

Settings, Look, Download themes lists the themes on GeekRhapsody/odyssey-themes
(themes.json and screenshots, a git repository cloned into the cache and
fetched when the page opens) and gets, updates and removes them as git clones
in ConfigDir/themes/<id>/ through LibGit2Sharp. Each entry pins the commit the
owner tested. Nothing loads or goes online at boot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

A theme switch frees the models the new theme doesn't use

Switching from Console to Slab kept Console's video memory until a
restart: models stayed for the session, and a dropped C# wrapper keeps
its native object until its finaliser runs, which SustainedLowLatency
can put off indefinitely.

- ModelLoader.ReleaseUnused disposes every unused model's mesh, textures
  and clips and frees its node tree once the grids hold the new
  templates (per-game models are left to ReleasePerGame).
- ItemGrid.SetTemplates disposes the old materials and MultiMeshes; the
  warm-up's go when it ends; the parked details ModelView drops its model.
- A second after a switch, a background full collection releases the
  textures and arrays held by SetShaderParameter's Variant disposers.

Console -> Slab now lands at 318-326 MB of Godot video memory (a fresh
Slab start: 295.7 MB) instead of 468.8 MB, steady over four round trips;
the same on Vulkan.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Version 0.16.0

An All games card joins Favourites and Recently played

Every visible game of every enabled system in one list, third at the start
of the systems grid (id all_games), in [display] games_sort's order. Each
game keeps its own system's template and shows its system's name. The list
is cached like a system's and read again when the sort changes or a game
ends under a play-based sort; its subtitle counts the library's games.

Core: GetAllGamesAsync (a system's sorted query without the system
condition) and GetAllGameMediaAsync (every game's media by kind in one
query, instead of chunks of 500 ids).

Themes give it a card and logo as the other two ([systems.all_games],
logos/all_games.*). Slab's is ES-DE's all-games collection image, supplied
by the owner; tools/slab-logos.py renames auto-allgames. The scroll bench
takes --bench-system=all_games.

Scrolling the 14,215 synthetic games end to end matches PS2's 10,000
(export, Slab, 3 runs each): scroll p99 16.98-17.00 ms against
16.97-17.00, no hitches, 96 B main-thread allocation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Wonderswan models
neutral light on default theme

Grids no longer fade items at the top and bottom of the screen

The item shader faded items near the screen's top and bottom into the
background gradient's colour, so over a bright background the rows under
the overlay washed out to that colour instead of darkening. The fade is
gone (edge_fade, ItemGrid.FadeAtEdges, and the inspected cell's exemption
in its per-cell data); only the overlay's dark scrims lie over them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
update gitignore

Themes set the focused item's sway and the others' bob

[motion] focus_sway and idle_bob (A6 Motion): multiples of the launcher's
own motion, 0 to 3, each the theme's else the base's else 1. The sway
scales ItemGrid.FocusTransform's angle; the bob is the item shader's
idle_bob uniform, set on a grid's materials only when it isn't 1. Both
grids and a system's details follow the theme, at boot and on a switch.

Benched before and after on the export (docs/perf/theme-motion.md): no
change in start-up, scroll frame times, GPU time, allocation or memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Menus perf: a used menu font leaves no memory behind

The 8 MB of video memory in scenario B was Godot counting D3D12MA's
heap blocks, not memory in use: section D measures it (10 runs each,
and 40 switches in a row with and without a font), with the data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Themes set their menus' colours and font; Slab goes dark grey

A theme's [ui.menu] sets the menus' background, text, accent and font
(A6 Menus). Setting no colour keeps the launcher's own palette exactly
(MenuPalette.Legacy); setting any derives every menu colour from the
three. UiStyle.Apply recolours the shared styles in place, with the
Godot Theme silent until all its boxes have changed, and maps the
colours the menus shown copied, so a switch applies with the settings
open. A font loads on a worker (at most 4 MB) and its ASCII is drawn
ahead at the menus' main sizes.

Slab's background is now black to dark grey, and its menus dark grey
with a light grey focus. Scrolling is unchanged; a palette switch costs
one 18-20 ms frame (docs/perf/menus.md).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Choose SteamGridDB's art in manual matching

Choosing a SteamGridDB result in "scrape this game" now opens an art
chooser when the game has several images of a wanted kind: a step per
kind (cover, logo, hero), each a grid of up to 12 images in the order a
scrape takes them, with "Keep this one" first when the game has a file.
The chosen image is downloaded in full and replaces the game's file of
that kind (as the user's own image does), then the game is scraped.

- Core: IScraper.ArtOptionsAsync, SteamGridDbScraper.ArtOptions (Parse
  takes the first of each), ScrapeService.GetArtChoicesAsync,
  GetArtThumbAsync and ScrapeGameWithMatchAsync with chosen images,
  UserArtService.SetAsync from bytes.
- App: GameArtPanel, GameMatchPanel opens it, Thumbnails.FromBytes,
  --open=art for captures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Game videos on game templates, and a 1990s CRT television

A game template can now play the focused game's own video, with its
sound, on one of its slot faces: [templates.<id>] video names the slot
and video_delay_ms (default 1000) how long the game is focused first.
The video fades in over the slot's art, loops, and stops when the focus
moves, the game launches, the grid hides or the UI layer opens.

Every game drawn with a template shares its material, so a card video's
texture swap would show on all of them. The item shader instead gets a
video_frame sampler and a video_state (cell, slot, aspect, fade) per
material, so only the focused cell's face shows it and the template
stays batched, with no new variant. Playback goes through the details
screen's VideoPlayback; games' videos are only read when a template the
theme uses plays them.

Memory Card gets crt_tv_90s (Tools/CrtTvBuilder: 782 triangles, two
materials), its screen the screenshot slot fitted whole, playing the
video after a second. It's assigned to no system.

Benches (docs/perf/game-videos.md): frame times unchanged; while a
640x480 video plays, render CPU +0.17 ms, working set +53 MB, video
memory +3 MB; on a system without the TV, before and after match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wait for background work calling into Godot when quitting

A quit while the theme's models were still converting on the thread pool
crashed the process in Godot's interop (17 of 24 early-quit captures).
Boot/GodotWork counts work that calls into Godot: new work is refused once
the app quits, and Main._ExitTree waits up to 5 s for the rest. Model
conversions, the boot's media arrays, thumbnails, the match panel's covers
and both video threads go through it (replacing the card video's own wait).
After: none of 24, waiting 14-203 ms.

Favourites and Recently played cards: a Power Star and the Dreamcast clock

Themes can now give Favourites and Recently played cards of their own
([systems.favourites] and [systems.recently_played] model), resolved like
a system's card; the default card stays their fallback. The console theme
uses it: Super Mario 64's Power Star (its focused clip opens its eyes,
hops, spins and wiggles) and the Dreamcast settings menu's alarm clock
(its focused clip bounces, rings and leaps), built by
tools/console-models/power_star.py and alarm_clock.py with the shared
clip.py. Also ignores __pycache__ and untracks a committed .pyc.
